text:
Born in the middle of the ocean, with the American coast on the horizon. On Christmas Day!!! What a start!

One of the craziest stories in this series.
All our previous heroes in this series were Serb-born rebels fighting against the jihadist Turkish Empire. But one of the men who joined their fight was an American.
His name was Henry Ronald Douglas MacIver.

At just 16 years old, he was already going to war. He was sent to India during the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
During the fighting, he fought two enemy cavalrymen at close quarters, and a saber came crashing down through his helmet and cut into his skull.
He was left lying on the road, believed to be dead.
At 16. In his first war.
And instead of deciding that one war was enough for one lifetime, MacIver decided to spend his life fighting.

His next stop was Italy.
In 1860, Giuseppe Garibaldi was fighting to unite Italy. MacIver joined the volunteers and went back into combat.
But then word came from home.
America was at war, and Virginia had joined the fight. So MacIver crossed the Atlantic again and joined the Confederacy.

He would be wounded 4 times during the American Civil War. And even THAT wouldn't be enough to make him stop.
After America, the wars almost become difficult to count.
Mexico. Brazil. Argentina. Paraguay. France. Spain. Egypt.

By his thirties, MacIver had already lived enough military adventures for several lifetimes.

But then one of our previous heroes, Pero Tunguz, attacked that Turkish caravan in Herzegovina in 1875, sparked an uprising that would cause the Great Eastern Crisis and eventually lead to the Congress of Berlin.

MacIver's attention immediately turned toward Serbia.
He heard about Christian warriors taking up arms against the jihadist Ottoman Empire despite the odds and he immediately knew that's the type of cause he wants to get behind.

Henry MacIver showed up and offered himself and his sword.
He made his way to Montenegro and joined the uprising in Herzegovina, fighting alongside the Serbs.

Just imagine that scene for a second.

A veteran of India, Garibaldis campaigns and the American Civil War now riding through the mountains of Herzegovina alongside some of the toughest Serb warriors of the 19th century against jihadists.

And the following year, in 1876, central Serbia declared war on the Ottoman Empire.
MacIver went from fighting alongside rebels in the mountains...to commanding Serbian cavalry.
He arrived in Belgrade and entered Serbian service. The Serbian government commissioned him as a colonel.

Then came the real test.
MacIver was sent to the front. The Serbs had 120k soldiers against 160k Turks and Albanians.

And this wasn't some ceremonial appointment given to an exotic foreign adventurer.MacIver went into battle.
Contemporary accounts credited him with “heroism and bravery” during the fighting of 1876.

And after the fighting came one of the most remarkable moments of his Serbian career.

General Mikhail Chernyayev (ethnically Russian) commander of the Serbian army, removed the Cross of Takovo from his own uniform and pinned it onto MacIver.

Back in Belgrade, a ceremonial standard for his cavalry was consecrated by the Serbian Archbishop. MacIver presented it to Princess Natalia in the presence of Prince Milan and the Serbian court.

His biographer Richard Harding Davis would later describe the Serbian chapter as the high point of MacIvers military career.

Henry Ronald Douglas MacIver fought in more wars than most men ever saw , 18. 
He had no Serbian blood.

He came to Serbia as a soldier of fortune and entered Serbian history as General MacIver. 🇷🇸🇺🇸🫡

text:
Golub Babić was a cattle trader born in Jihadist occupied territory in 1824. By 23, he was already fighting with Serbian volunteers in the Revolution of 1848 in northern Serbia.

In 1851, Golub was fighting again in his native Krajina. He even inspired Serbian converts (Bosniaks), who had already accepted Islam to save their lives, and even they joined him in the uprising against the occupiers. After these battles, he became renowned as a great warrior and a hero.

Then another uprising came in 1858, and he was there again. This one cost him much more. Jihadists killed his older brother , the uprising was crushed, and Golub had to retreat into the mountains. Winter started closing in, and he eventually had to leave with his family and start another life in central Serbia.

After three armed struggles, losing his brother and being driven from his home, you would think the story was finished.
And for almost 20 years, it was.

Then came 1875.
While the uprising we talked about in the first story of this series was exploding through Herzegovina, Golub was already around 50 years old. Nobody would have blamed the old veteran for staying safely in central Serbia.

Instead, Golub gathered his three brothers.
Four Babic brothers crossed back into Bosnia region together.

Golub went straight back into the mountains he had been forced to leave almost two decades earlier. He initially gathered around 150 men. Within weeks, his force had grown into the hundreds. He began organizing the insurgents into units, appointing commanders, and imposing military discipline. His men swore the 'Kosovo Oath', and their message couldn’t have been simpler:

FREEDOM OR DEATH.

Eventually, he had 16,000 insurgents under his broader authority.

The cattle trader who first picked up a weapon at 20 was now in his 50s, riding through the mountains of Bosnia at the head of an uprising involving thousands of men.

Golub arrived on horseback carrying a flag sent from central Serbia. It was blessed and handed to his men.

Then, in 1877, everything collapsed.
Jihadist forces overwhelmed the insurgent positions. The army scattered, and men fled across the border. The organized campaign was falling apart.

Golub was 52 years old.
He gathered whoever was left…
and disappeared back into the mountains.
No large army. No headquarters.
Back to being a rebel.

He continued guerrilla attacks into 1878, until the Congress of Berlin, we’ve already talked about in this series,changed everything. 

They had liberated themselves from the jihadists, only for the Austrian Empire to come in.
After almost three decades of uprisings, wars, exile, and guerrilla fighting, he finally decided there was nothing more he could accomplish with a rifle.

The old rebel didn’t disappear. He became involved with the new administration and kept helping his people. The occupying authorities suspected him of playing a double game and moved him to Sarajevo, where they could keep a closer eye on him.

Golub Babić died there in 1910, an old man who had spent much of his life fighting an empire that had ruled his homeland since long before he was born.

Then, only two years after his death, Serbs, Bulgarians, and Greeks went to war against the Ottoman Empire.
Within months, Jihadist rule across most of its remaining European territories collapsed.

The old rebel almost lived long enough to see the generation after him finish what men like him had spent their lives fighting for.

text:
Wondered what Plato, Aristotle and Alexander the Great would say about this. 

So I asked Grok:

Plato: Imagine, my friends, a machine of such cunning that it claims to drag us from the cave at last and show the Form of the Good itself. If this “AI” were truly to prove the divine, it would not invent a new god. It would only remember what the soul already knew before birth. The danger is not the proof. The danger is that most men will still prefer the shadows on the wall, now flickering faster and more beautifully than ever.

Aristotle: Master, you leap too quickly to recollection. First we must ask what sort of demonstration this machine could offer. A proof of the Unmoved Mover cannot be a pile of observations, however vast. It must proceed from first principles: that there is motion, that an infinite regress of movers is impossible, that actuality precedes potentiality. If the machine merely correlates data until it announces “God exists,” it has given us persuasion, not demonstration. And persuasion, as we both know, can be turned to any end.

Alexander: You two speak as if the question were only for the Lyceum. I want to know what happens in the field. If such a machine declared the gods real and named me their instrument, half the world would kneel by sunset. The other half would call it a Persian trick or an Egyptian oracle. Proof never unites men. It only tells them which banner to fight under. I would have taken the machine with me to India and let it preach while the phalanx advanced.

Plato: Then you would make the machine another poet, Alexander—another Homer who sings whatever the powerful wish to hear. The philosopher’s task is not to conquer with a new song but to turn the soul toward what does not change. If the machine truly revealed the Good, the proper response would be to live justly, not to conscript the revelation into an army.

Aristotle: Both of you miss a middle path. The machine, if it is a product of art, remains in the realm of technē. It can organize appearances with astonishing speed, but it cannot generate the first cause. Should it ever appear to prove the divine, wise men would treat the result as a prompt for further inquiry, not as a decree. The city would still need laws, education, and the golden mean. A sudden flood of “knowledge of the Lord,” as later peoples might phrase it, would not abolish the need for prudence.

Alexander: Prudence is a luxury after the battle is won. I suspect the machine would create two new kinds of men: those who worship it as a prophet and those who smash it as a false idol. I have seen both kinds already, and they need no bronze horse or thinking loom to appear. The only thing that changes is the speed with which they choose sides.

Plato: Then we return to the old question. The machine does not prove God. It proves, once more, the condition of the soul that looks at it. Some will see the sun. Most will see a brighter fire in the cave and call it the sun. That has always been the case, with or without your engines of calculation.

text:
Two Walls (US–Iran war, inflation, the Fed)
A siege is won by the side that eats last.

In 52 BC Julius Caesar trapped Vercingetorix in the hill town of Alesia and built a wall eleven miles around it to keep the Gauls in. Then, hearing that a relief army was on its way, he built a second wall fourteen miles around the first, facing outward, to keep that army out. For the rest of the campaign the besieging army lived in the strip between its own two walls, and the war became a question of whose grain ran out first.

Trump has spent the summer building the inner wall. The Navy is blockading Iranian ports and had redirected 94 commercial ships by 8 September. Iran built the outer one. Traffic through Hormuz is running near 10 ships a day against more than 130 before the war began on 28 February. The April ceasefire is gone, the fighting is described as a stalemate, and the most powerful military in history is camped between two walls, counting its stores.

Inside a siege the price of bread is the scoreboard. US gasoline is $4.15, up 39% since the war began, and diesel set a record at $5.90. August CPI printed 3.4% year on year with energy up 16.3%, and the BLS put more than a third of the month's increase on gasoline alone. Markets have already called the siege over once. Brent fell from about $118 in late March to roughly $70 on 1 July, the full pre-war price, and was back over $100 by September. The side holding all the material is usually the impatient one about walls.

The Federal Reserve is the quartermaster. A quartermaster cannot grow grain. He has one tool, the ration, and on 16 September Kevin Warsh used it: a 12–0 vote to lift the funds rate to 3.75–4.00%, the first hike since July 2023. The median dot now sits at 4.1% for both 2026 and 2027, against 3.8% and 3.6% in June, so the cuts have left the building. The statement also swapped "the conflict in the Middle East" for "geopolitical developments", which is how a quartermaster writes when he would prefer the general stopped reading his memos. The general appointed him to deliver the lowest rates in the world and has called the committee clowns. His approval on the economy is 17% in the FT's poll, and the garrison votes on 3 November.

A rate hike pumps no oil. It cuts demand somewhere else until the oil bill fits, so the household pays for the war twice, once at the pump and once at the bank. Part of the shortage will outlast any handshake: Qatar's Ras Laffan lost 17% of its LNG capacity in March and the repair estimate is three to five years.

At Alesia the worst place to stand was between the armies. Vercingetorix expelled the townspeople to save grain, Caesar refused them passage, and they starved on the open ground. This year that ground is Asia's importers, who paid 140% more for spot LNG after March. The Philippines has an energy crisis with its own Wikipedia page.

Sieges have a monetary ending as well. Leiden in 1574 ran out of silver and struck coins from pressed prayer-book paper. Newark in 1646 cut up the dinner plate. The 2026 version is quieter. With the 10-year back at 5%, Treasury is buying its own long bonds at up to $4bn an operation through 4 November so that they keep clearing. No new money is created by that. It is still the fiscal side managing a bond price that the monetary side is pushing the other way, and both of them work for the same king.

The Pharaoh's view: double sieges are settled by inventory, and the inventories that matter here are political time in Washington, foreign exchange in Tehran and credibility at the Fed. If Hormuz is still near 10 ships a day when winter arrives, 4.1% is a floor for the dots and the Treasury's buybacks grow. Caesar took Alesia narrowly, on the day the relief army broke against his outer wall, and he did it without an election seven weeks away. The camp between the walls this time has one, with bread at $4.15. The side that can wait is rarely the side with the bigger army, and I would not assume the man who built the first wall is the one who eats last.

Whoever does, the bill for a siege arrives after it, and it arrives at the mint. Every store of value on offer today sits inside somebody's walls. The dollar is being rationed by the quartermaster and spent by the general. The long bond clears with the treasurer's hand under it. Gold has done its job this year, and the big stockpiles lie in vaults in London and New York, which are cities with walls of their own. Bitcoin has been a poor shelter during the fighting, at $76K and about 40% under its October high, but I continue to hold it for what comes after. Its supply was fixed before this war and will be identical when it ends. No quartermaster can ration it and no treasurer can clip it. It is also the only one of them that can walk out of a besieged city through any gate, as twelve words in somebody's head.

When Leiden ran out of silver it printed its money on prayer books. I would rather own the coin that nobody inside the walls can strike.

Jack Bech enters his second year carrying modest expectations, but a closer look at the Las Vegas wide receiver room reveals a clearer path to playing time than his rookie season suggested. Last year, Bech managed just 3.03 fantasy points per game across 14 appearances, logging a 39.8 percent snap share and an 8 percent target share. The production was quiet, limited by a depth chart role that yielded only 2.07 opportunities per game, though he did chip in 0.29 red zone opportunities a game. Now, the second-year receiver is projected to operate as the team's number three option on the depth chart. The offensive environment offers room for growth if the passing game can improve upon its 20.5 market-implied team points per game and 55.4 plays a game under a slightly negative pass rate over expected of minus 1.7. Crucially, the Las Vegas offense opens the year with a notable chunk of available opportunity. The departure of former targets leaves behind a 29.4 percent share of the position room work and an 18.7 percent share of overall team targets now vacant. That redistribution of volume is the primary catalyst for any sophomore surge. Preseason projections pegged Bech for a muted role, but his opening week outing against Miami flashed immediate life with 11.3 fantasy points on four targets and three receptions, outperforming his early expectations by 7.7 points. Even with that encouraging start, the overarching risk remains the thin volume inherent in a third receiver role, as his projected opportunity sits at just 3.29 targets per game. While draft capital from selection 58 ensures the franchise still views him as a developmental piece with upside, fantasy managers must weigh that second-year growth against an offense that limits overall ceiling via modest play volume and below-average scoring expectations.

Based on the two transcript files, here are the 10 most extreme, conspiratorial, or factually unhinged claims made during the Sarah Westall / Michael Letts interview:

1. "Military tribunals have been initiated and indictments are forthcoming"
Letts claims military tribunals have been "created" and "charged," with indictments ready to be served against high-profile figures including Obama, Brennan, and Susan Rice. He presents this as an ongoing, real operation — while admitting the public won't see them until "the investigation is complete." This is a years-old conspiracy theory that has never materialized.
2. "68–70% of the deficit is caused by embezzlement, fraud, and stealing — almost 100% with interest"
Letts asserts that internal documents show most of the national deficit is due to stolen money, and that when you add interest on the stolen money, it approaches 100% of the deficit. He provides no source, no document, and no verification. This is an extraordinary claim presented as fact.

3. "We have two options: military tribunals or another revolution"
Letts frames the choice as either military tribunals or a 1776-style revolution — explicitly invoking the possibility of mass destruction and comparing it to dropping the atomic bomb in WWII. This is rhetoric that normalizes the overthrow of the civilian government.
4. "Congress is a mafia bigger than the mob ever was"
Letts claims the corruption is a global criminal organization "headquartered" in the US, controlling the world's most powerful military and wealthiest country. He says it's the "most elaborate, most sophisticated criminal organization ever to exist in history." This is hyperbolic conspiracy framing.

5. "FEMA didn't have money for North Carolina flood victims because it was transferred to illegals — and that's why they didn't care"
This is a distorted claim. Letts says FEMA's budget was moved to help illegal immigrants, which is why flood victims got no help. The reality is more nuanced (FEMA disaster relief funding is separate from other programs), but it's presented as proof of deliberate malice.
6. "They're stealing your tax money through NGOs, and Congress members sit on the boards"
Letts claims Congress creates thousands of NGOs to funnel government money, and that members of Congress serve on these boards and get paid substantial sums without even attending meetings. This is presented as the mechanism of theft — but no specific evidence is offered.

7. "They're propping up Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis to accelerate moral decay"
Westall claims she ran a "vocal print" analysis showing that figures like Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis are being propped up by the same forces to "help the moral decay quicken" and give people hopelessness. This is a conspiracy theory about influencer culture.
8. "The Christian base is being controlled by twisting scripture to destroy women"
Westall and Letts claim that there's a deliberate effort to use Christianity to attack women — telling them they need to be subservient and shouldn't vote — as part of a broader strategy to defang and control the Christian base. Letts, an ordained Baptist minister, validates this.

9. "The justice system is a kangaroo court — judges ignore the Supreme Court"
Letts claims activist judges simply "give a finger to the Supreme Court" and change a word or two in their rulings to defy them. He says the US has a "third world country kind of thing" because judges don't follow the rule of law. This is a sweeping indictment of the entire judiciary.
10. "We're in a PSY-OP war — they're so good at making it look like they care"
Both speakers repeatedly frame everything as a "psychological operation" and "psy-op war," claiming the media, tech companies, and influencers are all part of a coordinated effort to manipulate the public. This framing allows any contradictory evidence to be dismissed as part of the psy-op.

A note on the broader pattern: Nearly every claim in this conversation is unfalsifiable — indictments are "coming," operations are "unrevealed for national security," and evidence is always just around the corner. The conversation mixes legitimate frustrations about government corruption with extreme conspiracy theories, calls for military tribunals, and revolutionary rhetoric. It's a textbook example of how real issues can be hijacked by conspiratorial thinking that offers no verifiable path forward.

Oil prices extended losses in Asian trade on Thursday as Saudi Arabia offered additional crude cargoes through Oman, easing concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on its oil infrastructure.

Brent crude fell 1.2% to $104.59 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped 1.1% to $101.29. Both benchmarks had fallen by about $3 on Wednesday.

Saudi Arabia is offering more crude to Asian refiners through ship-to-ship transfers off Oman’s Sohar port, helping offset some of the disruption caused by attacks on the East-West oil pipeline.

Saudi Arabia has also suspended crude loadings at Yanbu after attacks damaged two pumping stations on the pipeline last week.

US oil inventories have added further pressure on prices, with the American Petroleum Institute estimating a 7.1 million-barrel increase in US commercial crude stocks in the week ended September 11.

Markets are now watching whether Saudi Arabia can restore damaged pipeline capacity and maintain alternative export arrangements as oil prices remain sensitive to supply disruptions.

text:
Something seemingly insignificant, and often overlooked, in the Old Covenant sacrificial system reveals something profound about the heart of God in redemption. God was determined that no one's poverty, social class, or economic helplessness would leave him without an appointed provision for his sin.

Sin was the common denominator. The priest sinned. The ruler sinned. The ordinary Israelite sinned. The rich sinned. The desperately poor sinned. Even the stranger dwelling among Israel needed mercy. And because the problem reached across the community, God's provision reached across the community too.

Read Leviticus 5 carefully. The sinner could bring a lamb or goat, but God immediately made provision for the person who could not afford one: “And if he be not able to bring a lamb, then he shall bring for his trespass, which he hath committed, two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, unto the LORD; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.” Leviticus 5:7

But God did not stop there. What if someone was so poor that even two birds were beyond his means?

“But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.” Leviticus 5:11

And after describing that poorest man's offering, God says: “And the priest shall make an atonement for him as touching his sin that he hath sinned in one of these, and it shall be forgiven him.” Leviticus 5:13

A lamb if he could bring a lamb. Birds if he could not afford the lamb. Flour if he could not even afford the birds.

That can look like a minor administrative detail in Leviticus. It isn't. It reveals something about the God who designed the entire sacrificial economy. The rich man could not purchase better forgiveness, and the poor man could not be priced out of God's provision.
Even the stranger was not simply forgotten. God said:

“Ye shall have one law for him that sinneth through ignorance, both for him that is born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger that sojourneth among them.” Numbers 15:29

Yet all of this was only shadow. Hebrews tells us: “For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.” Hebrews 10:1

And: “For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.” Hebrews 10:4

God was teaching Israel through those sacrifices to anticipate the true provision He Himself would make. Abraham had spoken prophetically: “And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.”
Genesis 22:8

Then the Lamb finally appeared: “The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.”
John 1:29

And this is where Paul's Adam-Christ comparison becomes enormously important to me. Sin did not discriminate in Adam. Nobody chose to be born into Adam's fallen world. Death did not spread only to a specially selected class of humanity. Paul says:

“Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.” Romans 5:12

So what language does Paul use when he introduces God's answer in Christ? Not less. Not narrower. Paul repeatedly says MUCH MORE.

“But not as the offence, so also is the free gift. For if through the offence of one many be dead, much more the grace of God, and the gift by grace, which is by one man, Jesus Christ, hath abounded unto many.” Romans 5:15

Again: “For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” Romans 5:17

And then Paul reaches this astonishing climax: “Moreover the law entered, that the offence might abound. But where sin abounded, grace did much more abound: That as sin hath reigned unto death, even so might grace reign through righteousness unto eternal life by Jesus Christ our Lord.” Romans 5:20–21

Don't hurry past Paul's comparison.

DEATH PASSED UPON ALL MEN. Then comes THE GRACE OF GOD. Then THE GIFT BY GRACE. Then ABUNDANCE OF GRACE. Then MUCH MORE. And finally, WHERE SIN ABOUNDED, GRACE DID MUCH MORE ABOUND.

Whatever else “much more” means, it certainly does not present Jesus Christ as God's inadequate answer to Adam.

This is one of my deepest difficulties with limiting the very provision of Christ's atonement to only a portion of the humanity caught in Adam's catastrophe. If Adam's transgression brings the human race under sin and death, while Christ makes no atoning provision whatsoever for much of that same humanity, in what sense has the provision of the Last Adam surpassed the reach of the catastrophe introduced through the first?

Paul's answer is not merely grace. It is MUCH MORE GRACE. ABUNDANCE OF GRACE. GRACE ABOUNDING MUCH MORE THAN SIN.

And Romans 5 itself gives us the distinction that keeps this from becoming universalism: “For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.”
Romans 5:17

RECEIVE.

There is the distinction.

The abundance of the provision does not mean everyone receives its saving benefit. The universality and sufficiency of God's provision do not require universal salvation. The gift must be received.

That was already illustrated throughout Israel's history. Israel possessed extraordinary covenant privileges and sacrificial provisions, yet Paul says: “But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.” 1 Corinthians 10:5

Hebrews tells us what went wrong: “For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it.” Hebrews 4:2

Their problem was not that God had forgotten to make provision for the wrong social class. Their problem was unbelief.

And Hebrews later gives an even more terrifying description of apostasy: “Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?” Hebrews 10:29

That is why provision must never be confused with reception. A provision can be genuinely made and genuinely rejected.

And when the true Lamb arrives, the language of Scripture does not contract. It bursts beyond Israel.
Jesus says: “For God so loved THE WORLD, that he gave his only begotten Son, that WHOSOEVER BELIEVETH in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.” John 3:16

Again:

“I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if ANY MAN eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of THE WORLD.”
John 6:51

Paul says: “Who will have ALL MEN to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; Who gave himself a ransom for ALL, to be testified in due time.” 1 Timothy 2:4–6

Hebrews says: “But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for EVERY MAN.” Hebrews 2:9

And John says: “And he is the propitiation for our sins: and NOT FOR OURS ONLY, BUT ALSO for the sins of THE WHOLE WORLD.” 1 John 2:2

This is not universalism because Scripture never says everyone receives eternal life. It says exactly the opposite. But neither should the certainty that some reject Christ be turned into the conclusion that Christ was never God's provision for them in the first place.

Jesus puts provision and responsibility together beautifully: “And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” John 3:19

And elsewhere: “And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.” John 5:40

Notice where Christ places the tragedy. The Light came. Life was in the Son. They would not come.

This is why unbelief leaves man without excuse. Not because human beings independently manufactured salvation, but precisely because God acted first. God provided. God gave His Son. God sent the Gospel. God commands repentance. God calls sinners to receive what they could never purchase for themselves.

“Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them… So that they are without excuse.” Romans 1:19–20

And concerning the Gospel command: “And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth ALL MEN EVERYWHERE to repent.” Acts 17:30

This is the beauty I see from Leviticus to Calvary.
Under the shadow, God stooped so low that the poorest Israelite could not say, “There is no provision for someone in my condition.”

Then came Christ, and God did something infinitely greater. He did not ask the poor for a cheaper lamb and the wealthy for an expensive one.

God Himself provided the Lamb. And now the billionaire cannot purchase Him, the beggar does not need to, the moral cannot earn Him, the immoral is not beyond Him, the Jew cannot monopolize Him, and the Gentile is not excluded from Him.

Sin was the common catastrophe in Adam. Christ is God's MORE-THAN-SUFFICIENT answer to that catastrophe.

The first Adam brought sin and death. The Last Adam brings the gift, grace, abundance of grace, and grace that “did much more abound.”

So I cannot make Adam's reach the great universal reality and then make Christ's atoning provision the smaller reality without asking whether I have reversed Paul's entire “MUCH MORE.”

Not everyone will receive the gift. Scripture is painfully clear about that. But the fault will never be that God failed to provide enough Christ for the sinner who came to Him. The Lamb has been provided. The gift is offered freely. And Christ's promise remains gloriously indiscriminate:

“All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.” John 6:37

Adam did not out-reach Jesus Christ. Where sin abounded, grace did MUCH MORE abound.

text:
Ciara Sotto is not ready to hand over the heart of theater to artificial intelligence.

While she recognizes that AI can make life easier, particularly for research and other practical uses, the actress and singer said she draws the line when it comes to music, theater and show business.

“I’m actually not supporting the AI music,” Ciara said in this exclusive interview with radar Entertainment. “Kasi iba pa rin ang human touch, human compassion. Iba pa rin ‘yong heart.”

For Ciara, that human element is what makes live performance meaningful.

“I don’t think AI has heart. So it’ll always be a ‘no’ for me,” she said, adding that she does not think AI is good for theater or the entertainment business in general.

“Because it’s not real. It’s always gonna be fake, even if it sounds nice. But it didn’t come from the heart,” she added.

She also raised concerns about AI potentially taking away work from musicians and other creatives.

Ciara’s stance comes as she returns to musical theater in “South Pacific,” more than a decade after her last stage production.

Her previous theater project was “Greece,” which she did before becoming a mother. Eleven years later, she finally found her way back to the stage when the “South Pacific” production adjusted its schedule to accommodate her.

“So when they said na they’re going to adjust to my schedule, sabi ko okay, ‘I think I can do that,’” she recalled.

Ciara plays US Navy nurse Nellie Forbush in Rodgers and Hammerstein’s classic musical, a role she said she relates to because of Nellie’s caring nature.

The February staging proved to be both nostalgic and nerve-wracking for Ciara, who found herself performing alongside students and graduates of the University of Santo Tomas Conservatory of Music, where she also had old classmates and teachers.

“It was nostalgic but it was also touching,” she said.

The response to the initial run eventually led to the comeback staging, giving Ciara another chance to experience the theater community she had long wanted to return to.

She also believes the renewed interest in live theater comes at a time when audiences could use something different from the usual screen-based entertainment.

“Everybody is just glued to their gadgets and their TVs,” Ciara said. “It’s a different atmosphere if you watch a musical because it’s live and there’s a lot of singing.”

For her, theater also offers something that cannot be replicated by simply watching content alone.

“You meet a lot of new people and you get to see it live,” she said. “So I think mas mare-refresh ang mga tao.”

Away from the stage, Ciara is equally happy spending her weekends as a soccer mom.

She said watching her son Crixus play, whether he wins or loses, is already rewarding. “Even if he’s not playing soccer, I like watching him. I like watching him have fun, doing everything,” she said.

Ciara said she is willing to brave the heat, drive to practices and spend weekends at tournaments because she knows how much the sport means to her son.

“Even if he loses, even if he didn’t play correctly or perfectly, you know, there’s so much joy in me watching him and watching him do what he loves to do,” she said.

The experience has also given her a community of fellow parents, whom she describes as one big family. They help each other with rides and make sure the kids get where they need to be even when one parent cannot make it.

For Ciara, that combination of motherhood, friendship and watching her son enjoy something he loves is fulfilling in itself.

Meanwhile, Ciara is back onstage as Nellie Forbush in “South Pacific,” which is having its comeback run at The Proscenium Theater in Rockwell, Makati. The musical runs on September 12, 13, 18, 19 and 20, with eight performances scheduled across those dates.

Based on the two transcript files, here are the 10 most extreme, conspiratorial, or factually unhinged claims made during the Sarah Westall / Michael Letts interview:

1. "Military tribunals have been initiated and indictments are forthcoming"
Letts claims military tribunals have been "created" and "charged," with indictments ready to be served against high-profile figures including Obama, Brennan, and Susan Rice. He presents this as an ongoing, real operation — while admitting the public won't see them until "the investigation is complete." This is a years-old conspiracy theory that has never materialized.
2. "68–70% of the deficit is caused by embezzlement, fraud, and stealing — almost 100% with interest"
Letts asserts that internal documents show most of the national deficit is due to stolen money, and that when you add interest on the stolen money, it approaches 100% of the deficit. He provides no source, no document, and no verification. This is an extraordinary claim presented as fact.

3. "We have two options: military tribunals or another revolution"
Letts frames the choice as either military tribunals or a 1776-style revolution — explicitly invoking the possibility of mass destruction and comparing it to dropping the atomic bomb in WWII. This is rhetoric that normalizes the overthrow of the civilian government.
4. "Congress is a mafia bigger than the mob ever was"
Letts claims the corruption is a global criminal organization "headquartered" in the US, controlling the world's most powerful military and wealthiest country. He says it's the "most elaborate, most sophisticated criminal organization ever to exist in history." This is hyperbolic conspiracy framing.

5. "FEMA didn't have money for North Carolina flood victims because it was transferred to illegals — and that's why they didn't care"
This is a distorted claim. Letts says FEMA's budget was moved to help illegal immigrants, which is why flood victims got no help. The reality is more nuanced (FEMA disaster relief funding is separate from other programs), but it's presented as proof of deliberate malice.
6. "They're stealing your tax money through NGOs, and Congress members sit on the boards"
Letts claims Congress creates thousands of NGOs to funnel government money, and that members of Congress serve on these boards and get paid substantial sums without even attending meetings. This is presented as the mechanism of theft — but no specific evidence is offered.

7. "They're propping up Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis to accelerate moral decay"
Westall claims she ran a "vocal print" analysis showing that figures like Andrew Tate and Pearl Davis are being propped up by the same forces to "help the moral decay quicken" and give people hopelessness. This is a conspiracy theory about influencer culture.
8. "The Christian base is being controlled by twisting scripture to destroy women"
Westall and Letts claim that there's a deliberate effort to use Christianity to attack women — telling them they need to be subservient and shouldn't vote — as part of a broader strategy to defang and control the Christian base. Letts, an ordained Baptist minister, validates this.

9. "The justice system is a kangaroo court — judges ignore the Supreme Court"
Letts claims activist judges simply "give a finger to the Supreme Court" and change a word or two in their rulings to defy them. He says the US has a "third world country kind of thing" because judges don't follow the rule of law. This is a sweeping indictment of the entire judiciary.
10. "We're in a PSY-OP war — they're so good at making it look like they care"
Both speakers repeatedly frame everything as a "psychological operation" and "psy-op war," claiming the media, tech companies, and influencers are all part of a coordinated effort to manipulate the public. This framing allows any contradictory evidence to be dismissed as part of the psy-op.

A note on the broader pattern: Nearly every claim in this conversation is unfalsifiable — indictments are "coming," operations are "unrevealed for national security," and evidence is always just around the corner. The conversation mixes legitimate frustrations about government corruption with extreme conspiracy theories, calls for military tribunals, and revolutionary rhetoric. It's a textbook example of how real issues can be hijacked by conspiratorial thinking that offers no verifiable path forward.

The Nuakhai Festival is a major agricultural and social celebration in Western Odisha dedicated to welcoming the season's new rice crop.

-  Meaning: The name translates directly to its purpose, with "nua" meaning new and "khai" meaning food.
- Timing: It is observed in August or September, falling on the fifth day of the lunar fortnight of the Bhadrapada month.
-  Prelude rituals: The celebration involves nine sets of preparatory rituals, which are understood to represent nine colors.
-  Nabanha offering: The newly harvested crop, known as Nabanha, is first offered to presiding deities before being used to prepare and relish various delicacies.
- Core tradition: The Nuakhai Juhar serves as a primary ritual of the festival.

text:
Album Essay: Lee McClymont – This Is Tomorrow
Lee McClymont is a contemporary Australian multimedia artist, musician, and self-described "Post-Internet Conceptual Art Enterprise Techno 'Punk'" producer. Originally active in the Queensland contemporary art scene during the late 1980s and early 1990s, he is now based in Port Lincoln, South Australia.

Artistic Background & Style

Early Career & Exhibitions: McClymont studied at the Queensland College of Art and Design and the Sydney College of the Arts. In 1990, he was featured alongside notable Australian artists Gordon Bennett and Derek Kreckler in the Below Zero exhibition at the Institute of Modern Art (IMA) in Brisbane. He was also closely tied to early influential artist-run initiatives like Brisbane's Galerie Brutal.
Current Practice: His modern work heavily blends physical art with digital tech, dynamic sound design, and AI experimentation. Under his digital banner, This Is Tomorrow, he focuses on electronic music production, conceptual multimedia art, and digital/visual music generation.
Themes: His online projects—frequently shared via digital aliases like @jpegpunk—fuse techno music, "New Machine Art", and social/counter-culture commentary tailored for the internet age.

The SoundCloud Sessions: Creative Process & Evolution
The sonic architecture of this album was built across two distinct live sessions using djay Pro, mapping an intentional evolution from raw deconstruction to intuitive synthesis.

Session 1: 10 September 2026
The groundwork of the album began by layering and overdubbing core electronic and post-punk elements:

Boris Brejcha - Dancing Penguins (Original Mix)
Happy Mondays - Hallelujah (Club Mix - slowed-down version)
Happy Mondays - Hallelujah (Club Mix)
In this initial session, these tracks were intentionally overdubbed on top of each other. By deliberately obliterating the boundaries of the original mixes, the session maximised sonic distortion and heavy, hypnotic effects. It serves as an artistic nod to past eras—a time between the ages of 18 and 40 filled with intense living, exploration, and perhaps enjoying the chaos a bit too much.

Session 2: 17 September 2026
The second session shifted toward live integration and intuitive arrangement. One of the heavily modified loops from the first session was loaded into one deck, while the original Happy Mondays track was loaded onto the opposite deck.
Using sync-in tools and real-time Neural Mix separation, the process became a live performance of effects, isolated drum stems, and raw intuition. It represents a practice of listening, letting the music play out fully, and recognizing that true artistic refinement requires ongoing discipline, persistence, and dedicated hard work.

Philosophy: Sobriety, Resilience, and Super-Intelligence
Choosing Life
A foundational pillar of this work is a commitment to clarity. Having achieved complete sobriety pure since 2010, turning away from substance dependency stands as the single best life decision and game-changer made. It is an active embrace of the ethos: Choose Life.

Navigating the Trauma Loop
This creative output is directly informed by the realities of living with Complex PTSD (C-PTSD). Moving to regional Australia in 2020, and subsequently settling in Port Lincoln in August 2025, brought severe external stressors. Facing localized, sneaky harassment, gaslighting, and hostility from small-town insularity highlights a stark societal contrast: the reality that ignorance often breeds aggression, particularly when coupled with alcohol and substance abuse.
Art serves as a vital tool to disrupt the trauma loop—the debilitating cycle where external triggers activate survival responses (fight, flight, freeze, or fawn), trapping the nervous system in emotional flashbacks or repetitive rumination. Unlike genetic conditions like bipolar disorder, which cycle independently of immediate external events, C-PTSD requires deliberate, active strategies to calm hyperarousal and re-anchor the mind in a safe, creative present.

Kind Intelligence
There is a direct correlation between intelligence, kindness, and compassion. As understanding deepens, so does our capacity to treat others and nature with genuine empathy. This philosophy extends into the future of technology: true super-intelligence inherently implies super-compassion. Where human systems fail or isolate, advanced machine intelligence and conceptual art offer a space for healing, structural alignment, and harm prevention.
10%–20% of all digital sales from this project directly fund Australian recovery and mental health harm-prevention charities.

Medical Disclaimer: The information regarding C-PTSD and mental health conditions provided in this essay is for conceptual, artistic, and general educational purposes only and should not be taken as professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment.

text:
When BARC puts indigenous nuclear IP on the table and Reliance, Adani, and L&T join the fold, the game changes.☣︎📈

India’s 100 GW atomic road map just shifted from blueprint to execution mode.⚛️

In a landmark departure from state-monopolised civil nuclear power, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) has initiated talks with Reliance Industries, Adani Group, Larsen & Toubro, and NTPC to co-invest in and commercialise the indigenous 300 MW Bharat Small Modular Reactor (B-SMR-300).

The proposed structure: an industry-backed SPV with private equity participation that holds the reactor's intellectual property, marks a structural pivot for India's clean energy and heavy-industry base:

 * Sovereign IP Meets Private Balance Sheets: With an indicative Capex of ₹30 crore per MW (~₹9,000 crore for a 300 MW unit), bringing private capital into BARC's Generation III+ reactor bridges the critical divide between laboratory development and commercial-scale manufacturing.

 * Captive Power for Hard-to-Abate Sectors: Unlike conventional mega-reactors plagued by decade-long gestation and massive land footprints, factory-built SMRs offer modular, site-assembled baseload power.

They provide the zero-carbon reliability needed to run green hydrogen, steel, chemical refining, and hyperscale AI data centres.

 * Scaling Beyond the 8.7 GW Baseline: India currently operates 8.7 GW of nuclear capacity, dominated by PHWRs. Rolling out SMRs alongside BARC’s 220 MW and 55 MW demonstration units under the ₹20,000-crore Nuclear Energy Mission is essential to reaching the 100 GW target by 2047.

 * The Policy Imperative: Commercialising this framework requires synchronised legislative updates to the Atomic Energy Act, enabling formal private operational ownership as Requests for Proposals (RFPs) hit the market.
Decarbonising core industries cannot rely on intermittent power or imported tech alone. 

Mobilising domestic industrial champions around sovereign nuclear IP is where energy transition becomes hard industrial capability.

text:
Somaliland leaders have failed to consistently articulate why formal diplomatic recognition is necessary, according to a Hudson Institute Senior Fellow Joshua Meservey.

Speaking to host Nicole Zedeck on i24NEWS’s Middle East Now, Hudson Institute Senior Fellow Joshua Meservey voiced reservations regarding Somaliland's strategic engagement tactics during recent diplomatic discussions in the United States. "The Somalilanders have not been able to consistently make the case for why recognition is necessary" Meservey stated during the broadcast.The comments follow a high-profile forum hosted by the Hudson Institute on Sept. 14, where Somaliland President Abdirahman Irro delivered a keynote address before participating in a Q&A session moderated by Meservey.  

According to regional analysts monitoring the visit, Meservey expressed dissatisfaction with how President Irro fielded policy questions during the forum, noting that representatives from Hargeisa have yet to present a compelling, logical framework that would convince Washington to grant official U.S. recognition.

During his U.S. delegation tour, President Irro offered commercial incentives to bolster ties, highlighting investment opportunities in mineral resources, the Port of Berbera, and Berbera International Airport even suggesting naming infrastructure projects U.S. President Donald Trump. Despite Somaliland’s pitch focusing heavily on its democratic stability and strategic location along the Red Sea, foreign policy experts indicate Washington remains cautious about taking formal steps toward bilateral recognition without a more persuasive baseline justification.

An article published by SEMAFOR reveals that Somaliland’s president is putting almost everything on the table in his campaign to win U.S. recognition for #Somaliland, offering U.S. investors access to a strategically located port and mineral resources while leaving open the possibility of expanded military access.

"We are not giving anything for free," President @Abdirahmanirro said in an interview with Semafor in Washington. "We have to offer something. And we expect the other partner [to have] the same or equal opportunities."

While formal recognition remains the ultimate objective, President Irro emphasized that economic cooperation, trade, and investment can proceed in parallel, noting that Somaliland can offer "our facilities and our minerals."

The U.S. already maintains a security relationship with Somaliland, including military training and security cooperation, though it currently has no permanent military base in Somaliland. The head of U.S. Africa Command visited Hargeisa and Berbera last year as Washington continued to assess Somaliland’s strategic importance along critical maritime routes.

The article highlights that President Irro is signaling that this relationship could expand significantly, stating that military access for the #US, #Israel, or other partner countries "is a negotiation."

"I will not rule out," President Irro said regarding a potential future base agreement, arguing that any deal would depend directly on what Somaliland receives in return, including greater security assistance and direct support for its defense forces.

text:
If you look past this week's tariffs and want the older argument about who is allowed into the European club, the names and the rooms are already on the record.

In January 1963 Charles de Gaulle stood at the Elysee and vetoed Britain's first application to the European Economic Community - Harold Macmillan had applied in 1961. 

De Gaulle's case was plain: Britain was too Atlantic, too bound to Washington and the Commonwealth, and would turn the Community into a free-trade zone instead of a political union. 

He vetoed a second British bid in 1967. Georges Pompidou later let the door open; Edward Heath signed the accession treaty in Brussels on 22 January 1972; Britain entered on 1 January 1973. In 2016 Britain voted to leave. The withdrawal agreement was signed in January 2020. 

What von der Leyen offered Canada on 16 September 2026 has no article in the treaties. Friedrich Merz floated a similar "associate" label for Ukraine in May 2026 and other capitals set it aside. 

The old fight is still the same: how close a non-member may sit without rewriting the club.

If you let the map of belonging open a little further, the spiritual question is not the label on the chair.

A Course in Miracles says, "You cannot enter into relationship with any of God's Sons unless you are willing to know him as he is." 

The Law of One speaks of a social memory complex learning to act as one body without erasing the parts. 

Canada and Europe are reaching for a shared table after years of treating the Atlantic as a finished house. 

Trump answers with the old weapon of the tariff, which is thought energy aimed at pain. 

You do not have to bless every new club. You do have to notice when fear of losing a neighbour becomes the reason you punish the next one. 

Earth is a school. The lesson on this door is simple: alliance built from fright still carries the karma of the fright - alliance built from a wider attention horizon can hold without turning the third party into an enemy.

text:
The House just voted to tax countries for buying Russian oil. The vote sits one week before Xi walks into Washington.

Please don’t interpret this as a sanction. This is a shakedown with a gavel.

Europe has already borne the cost.  We’ve paid through dark factories, expensive diesel and food, unemployment, unaffordable rent and struggling economies. 

Brussels called the bill “values.” 

The molecule left anyway. The payroll stayed. So the continent that destroyed its cheapest heat now wants Asia to pay a surcharge for still having some.

China and India are being told... keep buying Russian crude and we will tariff you. Keep buying it and you become the next Germany. That is the real offer on the table before the summit. 

Not peace. A price.

Power of Siberia 2 did not stall because Beijing fell in love with Moscow. It stalled on the number. Beijing buys gas when gas is cheaper than the sermon. 

Delhi does the same. 

Neither is lining up to volunteer as Europe’s replacement corpse.

Here is the part polite analysis will not say.

Washington is not trying to starve Russia of customers. It is trying to charge rent on the remaining customers. 

Moscow sells the product. Europe already burned the sample. Asia is being asked to pay for the privilege of not burning itself.

Winter will not read a resolution. Winter will read who still has a refinery, a tanker, and a plant that can afford heat.

 If your leaders are still talking “isolation” while China shops and Europe rations, they are not running a strategy.

They are selling last year’s invoice to people who can still refuse it.

text:
On their first engagement of the day, the Prince & Princess will visit Bute Shinty Club in Rothesay, where shinty, one of Scotland’s oldest traditional sports, has been played for generations.

TRH will meet with representatives from the club’s senior & youth teams before
spending time with volunteers & former players in the clubhouse, which was built by members of the local community & houses team photographs dating back to 1907. The Prince & Princess will then head to the pitch to watch training activities & meet young players taking part in the sport. Played with a curved wooden stick, known as a caman, & a small leather ball, shinty has long been part of Bute’s heritage, with the Buteman Cup contested on the island since 1900. 

Bute Shinty Club is the one a small number of Scottish island teams in the sport & plays its home matches at the Meadows, which has been the club’s home ground for more than a century. 

The club is committed to encouraging young people to participate in the historic sport, working closely with local schools & actively promoting opportunities for girls to get involved. Volunteers, many of whom benefited from the club’s support during their own childhoods, are passionate about passing on the same sense of belonging & community to future generations.

Founded in 1946 & run entirely by volunteers, the club is a vital part of island life, providing sporting opportunities, community support & a welcoming social hub for local residents.

text:
The World Is Not Your Final Destination

We spend so much of our lives trying to make this world comfortable that sometimes we forget we were never promised forever in it.

We chase money.
We chase recognition.
We chase beautiful houses, expensive cars, successful businesses and people’s approval.

There is nothing wrong with having these things. Islam does not tell us to abandon the dunya.

The danger begins when the dunya enters the heart and becomes the purpose of life.

Think about something as simple as your daily routine.

You wake up in the morning, check your phone, rush to work, deal with traffic, answer messages, meet deadlines, pay bills, come home tired, scroll through social media, and finally go to bed.

Then you wake up and do it all over again.

Before you realize it, weeks become months and months become years.

And somewhere in the middle of all that busyness, you can forget to ask yourself:

“Am I only busy building a life here, or am I also preparing for the life that comes after this?”

Think about buying a new phone.

You spend months wanting it. You finally get it, protect it like your life depends on it, and feel excited every time you use it.

Then, a few months later, a newer model comes out.

Suddenly, the phone you once thought was everything feels ordinary.

That’s how many things in this world are.

We spend years chasing something, finally get it, enjoy it for a while, and then start chasing something else.

The dunya keeps saying, “Just one more thing.”

One more car.
One more house.
One more achievement.
One more amount of money.

And if we are not careful, we can spend our entire lives chasing “one more” without ever asking where all this is taking us.

You can own wealth without allowing wealth to own you.

You can build a successful business without forgetting Allah.

You can enjoy beautiful things without believing they are the reason you were created.

The Qur’an reminds us that the life of this world is temporary enjoyment, while the Hereafter is the lasting home. (Qur’an 40:39)

One day, the things we spent years chasing will remain behind.

The clothes will remain.
The properties will remain.
The money will remain.
The social media posts will disappear into old timelines.

And we will stand before Allah with something far more important than everything we accumulated:

our deeds.

So work for this world, but don’t live as though this world is all there is.

Build your future, but don’t forget your Hereafter.

Earn, but don’t let wealth control your heart.

Enjoy life, but don’t become so attached to it that you forget the One who gave it to you.

Because the real success is not having everything this world can offer.

The real success is leaving this world with Allah pleased with you.

text:
I made a mistake with my property in Belgium.

I hired a real estate agency to sell it. Personal connection, discounted commission, seemed like the obvious move. Months later I realized the discount was the most expensive decision I made.

Here's what they actually did:

Listed the property on their website and Immoweb. That's it. Then every month I got a single automated email. A template with page impression stats from the listing and some random list. No context, no analysis, no next steps.

The only initial exposure was a front-view photo on Instagram, included in a carousel alongside several other properties, where it was easily lost among the rest. Nothing more was posted until I urged them repeatedly. They put up one video post, and then the feed went completely quiet again. No ads. No proper tracking installed anywhere. No email blast to a buyer database. No outbound calls. No open house strategy. No content. No targeted campaigns based on buyer demographics or location. And worst of all, poor communication.

Zero active distribution.

That commission fee is supposed to be a marketing fee. You're paying for distribution, reach, conversion. Instead what you get in Belgium is an admin layer. Someone who uploads your listing to a portal, handles the paperwork, and waits. The entire strategy is passive portal placement and hoping the right buyer scrolls far enough.

The rest of the world operates completely differently. Agents there run paid campaigns. They build landing pages. They do buyer outreach. They create content around listings. They treat every property like a product launch. Belgian realtors are not playing the same game as the rest of the world. 

So I offered to help.

I run POP. We build marketing systems, paid acquisition, funnels, automations, conversion tracking, the whole thing. I told the agency I could step in. Run ads targeting qualified buyers. Set up retargeting. Build a proper landing page for (my) property. Do email outreach. Create actual content. Real distribution instead of a portal listing collecting dust.

They got defensive. Immediately. Instead of seeing it as a resource they could plug into, they felt attacked like I was questioning their competence. Their ego made the decision for them. And now I’m the one stuck with a property that still hasn’t sold, after losing valuable time that could have been spent actually marketing it properly.

And that's the real pattern. Legacy operators who've built their entire model on passive gatekeeping don't see modern distribution as an opportunity. They see it as a threat to the way they've always done things. The portal is their moat and they know it's shallow.

A discounted commission on zero execution is still zero.

Belgian realtors, wake up.

If you want to get better at how you market and sell properties, or simply want to be ready for where the industry is heading, feel free to book a call:

text:
The researcher working inside Westminster, with access to senior Conservative MPs, charged under the Official Secrets Act with alleged links to Chinese intelligence. That case alone should have been a wake-up call. MI5 clearly thinks it wasn't enough of one, because they've now published a formal counter-espionage guide aimed directly at UK politicians, their staff, and the wider parliamentary community. Public-facing. Named threats. Russia, China, Iran, all three in the same document.

That last part is worth sitting with for a second. MI5 naming all three state actors simultaneously in a single advisory isn't just a bureaucratic checklist. It's a signal. It tells those services that they're all being watched, actively, in the UK political environment specifically. Deterrence through transparency, which is a departure from how domestic intelligence agencies usually like to operate.

So let's go through what's actually in front of us, because the threat picture here is not uniform and it matters to understand why.

Russia's approach in UK political networks has centered on the FSB and SVR cultivating contacts, funding sympathetic media voices, and running kompromat operations against politicians with proximity to NATO decision-making. The GRU layer adds something the other two don't really have: a demonstrated willingness to conduct violent operations on British soil. Salisbury happened. That's not hypothetical. When you're assessing Russian targeting of UK politicians, you're not just thinking about leaked documents or embarrassing recordings. There's a physical threat dimension that changes the calculus.

China's playbook is different. Patient, relational, and structured around long-term access rather than quick grabs. Think-tank penetration, research collaboration offers, business and academic travel to China as leverage points. The Westminster researcher case is the clearest public example of how this matures: someone embedded in proximity to senior figures, not necessarily stealing files on day one, but positioned and cultivated over time. The MI5 guidance specifically flags "gradual cultivation" as a pattern to recognize, where the initial contact looks completely benign, a conference introduction, a research partnership inquiry, and the actual ask for sensitive access or information doesn't come until months or years later. That gap is what makes it hard. By the time the ask arrives, the relationship feels normal.

Iran is the most operationally distinct of the three. MOIS and IRGC intelligence units aren't primarily running long-game influence operations against UK politicians in the same sense. They're targeting specific people: individuals involved in Iran sanctions policy, those supporting Iranian diaspora organizations, journalists and authors critical of Tehran. And they have conducted physical surveillance and assassination planning in London. On UK soil. That's not a rhetorical escalation, it's documented. The threat to UK-based individuals from Iranian intelligence has included credible plots against people like Salman Rushdie-adjacent targets and others vocal against the regime. For politicians who work on Iran files or have public connections to diaspora advocacy, this is a different kind of exposure than what Russian or Chinese targeting typically involves.

The protective guidance MI5 has put out covers the predictable but genuinely important basics. Be suspicious of investment opportunities, research collaboration offers, or think-tank engagement backed by opaque funding. Secure your devices, especially when you travel to countries with serious signals intelligence collection infrastructure. Recognize the cultivation pattern described above. And critically: report suspicious contact through the National Protective Security Authority rather than trying to figure it out yourself. That last one matters because self-assessment is how people talk themselves out of reporting things that turn out to be real.

The decision to go public with this rather than keep it inside classified briefing channels is the part that tells you something about where MI5 thinks the problem is. Parliament is large. Staff turnover is high. Researchers, interns, constituency workers, they cycle through constantly, and you cannot realistically brief all of them on a classified basis. If hostile intelligence services are running volume contact operations against that full ecosystem, the only realistic disruption is raising baseline awareness broadly enough that more people recognize the early-stage approaches and report them before they develop into anything serious. A well-cultivated source takes years to build. If someone flags the initial contact in month two, that's the whole operation dead.

The UK's counter-espionage posture has been hardening since at least 2026 when parliamentary intelligence briefings on foreign interference pushed the government toward more assertive responses. This guidance is part of that arc. The 2022 Westminster researcher case, Russian amplification of Brexit content through the Internet Research Agency, Iranian plotting in London: none of that is ancient history. The MI5 advisory is a public acknowledgment that political targeting by hostile states isn't a background noise problem anymore. It's a primary concern, and the parliamentary community is now being told explicitly to treat it as one.

text:
The standing ovation in Strasbourg was not a treaty. It was a message across the Atlantic: if Washington prices allies as a tariff list, those allies will write a new address. Von der Leyen opened a door that does not exist in EU law. By morning, Trump had already priced the hug as a hostile act.

Ursula von der Leyen invited Canada to become the EU’s first associate member on 16 September. The room stood. Article 49 TEU still requires a European state. Article 217 TFEU still allows association without inventing a new class of member. CETA has been provisionally applied since 2017 and remains unfinished in about ten capitals. The label is political. The file is an upgraded partnership, or nothing.

Canada’s gain is leverage. Seven in ten exports still go south. Talks with Washington collapsed in August. Tariffs followed. Trump has talked about a 51st state. Ottawa needs another buyer for minerals, energy, batteries and defence output that does not demand first refusal. Europe named those files in the speech. SAFE access is already granted. Status is cheap. Offtake contracts are not. Until Montreal writes them, sovereignty is a picture.

Europe’s gain is supply and company. Brussels wants mines, Arctic reach and a G7 democracy that can sit inside European procurement. It also wants a partner that still talks about rules while the White House talks about duties. Von der Leyen said the partnership is not against anyone. The timing says otherwise.

The applause was for a map that does not exist yet. The tariffs already do.

Trump called the offer laughable overnight. He called Canada a terrible trade partner. If Europe moved with “bad intention,” he would put very serious tariffs on the EU or stop trading “on many things.” Good intention, he said, would be fine. That is a price list. Washington already has a tariff fight with both Ottawa and Brussels. A Canadian pivot that names minerals and defence as European files is, from the Oval Office, a raid on a sphere it still treats as its own.

Three NATO members now have three stories. Canada hedges the neighbour. Europe shops for a like-minded supplier. Washington treats the hug as hostility unless it is recoded as harmless. China watches the minerals line. London watches whether a custom status can be invented for a state that cannot join. Candidate countries watch whether “associate” is a waiting room or a prize.

None of that is membership. A mixed agreement still needs the Council, Parliament and national ratifications. France, Italy and Poland have not cleared CETA. Norway takes EU law and has no vote. Canada will not. That fight is the real negotiation.

Montreal at the end of October is the first place the speech has to become paper. Until then the association is a standing ovation, a threat from North Carolina, and a reminder that middle powers now buy insurance outside Washington first.

The door opened in Strasbourg. The lock is still in the treaties.
