text:
We sampled 400 sub-niches for one client over 90 days.

Most fell off, a handful performed, but by the end we had something specific: 10 industries that convert, 17 ICP profiles that reply, four message types that work consistently across segments. That is not a guess or something our GTME landed on. That is a positioning statement the market built for us.

You cannot get there with project-based outbound: have a strategy, build a list, write angles, and send emails. Not because the work is necessarily bad. 

But, because the feedback loop is too slow and all human-centric.

A project answers one question. Did this campaign work? You scope it, build it, run it for six weeks, read the results, and start over. Four months per learning cycle. Meanwhile the list got hit by three other agencies running the same play and the angle that worked in month one is tired by month three.

A system answers a different question. What is actually true about this market?

You start with one ICP hypothesis and a few ways to position the offer. You do not pick the winner in a strategy session. You deploy all of them simultaneously and let the market decide. At 30,000 sends a day you get a statistically meaningful read on ten different angles in the time it takes a project shop to finish one campaign. The losing angles get killed automatically. The winning ones get promoted into a library that every future campaign inherits.

That library is the asset. 

After enough cycles it stops being a database and becomes a map. This is where the conversation lives in manufacturing. This is the vocabulary that lands in hospitality. This is the proof point that moves a CFO at a 200-person firm. None of it came from a whiteboard. All of it came from sending and reading what happened.

Signal-based outreach sits on top of this. And here is where most teams get it wrong.

They treat signals as a targeting filter. Find the trigger, fire the email. A funding round closes, you reach out. A VP of Sales gets hired, you reach out. That is better than random timing but it is not compounding. You are still guessing at the message.

The right model is different. The systematic layer already knows which angles work in that segment. The signal just determines when to fire a message that has already been proven. One bad campaign means the wrong message. Two bad campaigns means the wrong audience. The system already made those distinctions before the signal ever fired.

The BHL-Screener, formally e-screening, streamlines the collection and processing of Clinical Reminder questionnaires by automating Veteran outreach, response capture, CPRS Progress Note generation, and when applicable, completion of the Clinical Reminder. It reduces staff workload, minimizes variability in how questions are asked, and enables Veterans to complete important screenings before their appointments, thereby giving their primary care physician a more complete picture of the Veteran’s medical issues.

BHL Touch, a VA-approved web-based tool supporting measurement-based mental health care, now offers a new mode for Veterans to complete assessments anytime using their own device, in addition to traditional iPad entry in the office. This allows Veterans to receive and answer questions in advance of appointments, increasing the time they have with their primary care physician and reducing the time Veterans spend filling out paperwork when they arrive for their appointment. 

This new feature allows providers to text or email a secure link to a Veteran for convenient completion from anywhere. When the requested assessments are completed, the provider is immediately notified via email, and they can then review the results, track the patient’s progress over time, and seamlessly upload them to the electronic health record.

OH, MAMÍ @CandaceGuardian 

So we're going to have a little conversation about “Candace Owens the Great Debater.”

Because apparently the woman has been crowned the Queen of Debate by the Internet…

And I’m sitting here like:

¿PERDÓN? 🤨

¿DÓNDE ESTÁ EL DEBATE, MAMI?

Because when you actually look at the receipts, the picture is a LOT more complicated than:

“Candace will debate ANYBODY!”

Girl…

WILL SHE THOUGH? 😭

Let’s bring out the receipts.

🧾 RECEIPT #1: ANDREW WILSON

In 2026, Andrew Wilson offered $300,000 for a debate with Candace Owens over Charlie Kirk-related claims.

And this wasn't some little:

“Hey girl, wanna hop on Zoom?”

NO, SEÑORA. 😂

We are talking about a THREE-HUNDRED-THOUSAND-DOLLAR DEBATE PROPOSITION.

The negotiations became public, with Candace initially pushing for $500,000 before ultimately agreeing to the $300,000 figure under proposed conditions that included her studio and live fact-checkers. Reports also described Wilson as putting up the $300,000 connected to the event.

THREE. HUNDRED. THOUSAND. DOLLARS.

MAMÁ.

At that point, this isn't a debate.

THIS IS A CORPORATE EVENT. 😭💀

“Would you like to debate?”

“Of course.”

“How much?”

“Let me consult my accountant.” 😂

And THAT is why people are going to question whether the criticism of “pay-to-debate” is fair.

Because, Maya…

when the price tag starts looking like a down payment on a house, people are allowed to raise an eyebrow. 👀

🧾 RECEIPT #2: BEN SHAPIRO

Remember the whole Ben Shapiro situation?

Candace publicly challenged Ben Shapiro to debate her over Israel and the war in Gaza.

Shapiro offered to have that discussion on his show.

Candace declined that particular format.

Now, before somebody comes flying into my comments with a helicopter:

YES, I KNOW.

Candace has debated people.

She appeared on Jubilee's “1 Conservative vs. 20 Feminists.”

She has also appeared on Piers Morgan's program and participated in other confrontational interviews.

So no…

I'm NOT going to pretend she has literally never debated anyone.

The evidence doesn't support that.

But here's where the criticism gets interesting:

If you're going to build your entire brand around being the person who is fearless, intellectually unstoppable, and willing to debate anybody…

Then people are naturally going to notice when certain debates come with:

conditions, negotiations, preferred venues, money, fact-checking arrangements, or outright refusals of particular formats.

And THAT is where my Latina eyebrow goes:

⬆️

😂💅🏽

🧾 RECEIPT #3: TURNING POINT USA

And then we have the 2025 Turning Point situation.

Now THIS one deserves its own little telenovela chapter. 🎻

Because Candace Owens herself publicly challenged TPUSA and said:

“You can pick the place. You can pick the time. I say we do it tomorrow. We don't need to plan for this... I want it to be authentic.”

MAMI.

YOU SAID THAT. 😂💅🏽

Not me.

Not Erika.

Not Charlie's ghost.

YOU. SAID. IT.

You said:

“YOU PICK THE PLACE.”

“YOU PICK THE TIME.”

“LET'S DO IT TOMORROW.”

“I WANT IT TO BE AUTHENTIC.”

OH, SO WE'RE READY?

ANY PLACE.
ANY TIME.
TOMORROW.
KEEP IT AUTHENTIC.
Okay, reina.
LET'S GO. 🎤
And then…

TPUSA picked a place.

TPUSA picked a time.

TPUSA arranged an in-person broadcast from its Phoenix studio for December 15 and invited Candace to participate.

And suddenly…

THE VIOLINS STARTED PLAYING. 🎻🎻🎻

Because Candace subsequently objected to the in-person arrangement and offered a virtual alternative, while characterizing the planned event as a coordinated “character assassination” rather than the genuine open forum she said she wanted.

MAMÁ…

THE WHIPLASH. 😭

My neck just filed a workers' compensation claim.

Because yesterday:

“YOU PICK THE TIME!”

Then:

“YOU PICK THE PLACE!”

Then:

“LET'S DO IT TOMORROW!”

And then the calendar apparently arrived and said:

“Okay, girl. They picked one.”

😂😂😂

¿Y AHORA QUÉ?

🎭 ENTER: THE BIRTHDAY EXPLANATION

And THIS is where the telenovela gets extra spicy.

One explanation given for the December 15 date was that it was George Farmer's birthday.

Okay.

Fair enough.

A husband's birthday can absolutely be important.

Nobody is arguing with that.

BUT HOLD THE CAFECITO. ☕

Because when you actually look up George Farmer's birthday…

THE PUBLIC SOURCES DON'T EVEN AGREE WITH EACH OTHER. 😂

Some published biographies list George Farmer as born:

🎂 July 7, 1990

while other biography websites list:

🎂 December 15, 1989

Yes.

DECEMBER FIFTEENTH.

So now we're sitting here like:

“¿PERDÓN?!” 😭😂

Because apparently even George Farmer's birthday has entered the witness-protection program.

July?

December?

1989?

1990?

MAMÍ, SOMEBODY CALL THE BIRTH CERTIFICATE. 😂💀

And THAT is why I wouldn't make the argument:

“His birthday is definitely July 7!”

Because the public sources are inconsistent.

Instead, the question becomes:

WHY WAS DECEMBER 15 PRESENTED AS A SIMPLE, DEFINITIVE EXPLANATION WHEN THE PUBLIC RECORD ITSELF IS ALL OVER THE PLACE?

Now THAT is a legitimate question.

Because girl…

THE RECEIPTS ARE RECEIPTING, BUT THEY ARE ALSO ARGUING WITH EACH OTHER. 😂💅🏽

And let's go back to the original quote.

Candace didn't say:

“You can pick the place and time, provided the date doesn't conflict with my husband's birthday, the studio location, my podcast schedule, the weather, Mercury retrograde, and my preferred production arrangement.”

NOPE. 😂

She said:

“YOU CAN PICK THE PLACE.”

“YOU CAN PICK THE TIME.”

“I SAY WE DO IT TOMORROW.”

“I WANT IT TO BE AUTHENTIC.”

Mija…

YOU HANDED THEM THE CALENDAR. 📅

Then they wrote something on it.

And suddenly the calendar became controversial.

AYYYYY, DIOS MÍO. 😂

And before anybody gets dramatic in my comments:

No, this doesn't prove Candace is incapable of debating.

She has absolutely appeared in confrontational formats, including Jubilee.

THE GIRL CAN TALK.

Nobody needs to pretend otherwise.

The issue is something much narrower:

If you publicly demand an authentic debate and tell the other side to choose the time and place, people are naturally going to notice when the actual proposed format creates objections.

That's not persecution.

That's not misogyny.

That's not an attack.

THAT'S CALLED REMEMBERING WHAT YOU SAID YESTERDAY. 😂💅🏽

AND NOW…

Let's translate “scaredy-cat” for our international audience. 😂🌎

🇪🇸 Spanish:

GATITA ASUSTADA. 🐱

🇮🇹 Italian:

GATTINA SPAVENTATA. 😂🐱

🇷🇺 Russian:

ИСПУГАННАЯ КИСКА. 🐱

🇯🇵 Japanese:

怖がりな子猫 — kowagari na koneko. 🐱😂

And because we need one more language just to make this unnecessarily dramatic…

🇫🇷 French:

PETITE CHATTE EFFRAYÉE. 😂🐱

THERE.

The United Nations has been notified.

🤣🤣🤣

But here's my actual point, Mija:

Candace can debate.

She has demonstrated that.

Jubilee proves that.

Her interviews prove that.

Her public confrontations prove that.

So let's not make an argument that the receipts can't support.

The more interesting question is:

WHY DOES A SELF-PROCLAIMED FEARLESS DEBATER SO OFTEN NEED THE DEBATE TO HAPPEN ON PARTICULAR TERMS?

Because THAT is a legitimate question.

And when one debate involves a reported $300,000 offer, another proposed debate involves a preferred studio and live fact-checking, and another invitation was disputed over format…

MAMÁ…

THE MATH STARTS MATHING IN A VERY INTERESTING WAY. 😂☕💅🏽

Because debating isn't supposed to be:

“I will debate you, but first let me see the contract.” 😭

It isn't supposed to be:

“Who is moderating?”

“Where are we filming?”

“Can I bring my fact-checkers?”

“How much are you paying?”

“Can I approve the format?”

Girl…

At that point, I don't know if we're having a debate.

WE'RE NEGOTIATING A NETFLIX SPECIAL. 💀🎬

And THAT is where the Latina in me sits back, takes a sip of cafecito and says:

“Mija… si de verdad no le tienes miedo al debate, ¿POR QUÉ TANTO TRÁMITE?” 😂☕💅🏽

Because confidence doesn't need a parade.

It just needs a chair, a microphone, an opposing argument, and receipts.

And if the argument is strong?

LET IT FLY.

No smoke.

No theatrics.

No $300,000 circus.

Just:

“Okay. Sit down. Let's debate.”

🎤

NOW THAT'S A DEBATE. 💅🏽😂

🧾💀 AND THEN, MAMI… WE HAVE THE HOMEWORK PROBLEM.

Now let's talk about something else that matters when we're discussing debating.

Because before you walk into a debate, you have to know your material.

You have to read the documents.

You have to verify the evidence.

You have to know the difference between:

A TEXT MESSAGE.

A DISCORD MESSAGE.

AN INDICTMENT.

AND SOMETHING SOMEBODY SENT YOU ON THE INTERNET.

Because otherwise…

AY, DIOS MÍO. 😭☕💅🏽

You are basically walking into a debate wearing six-inch heels with NO SHOES ON YOUR ARGUMENT. 😂

And THIS is where the CNN interview with Elle Reeve becomes relevant.

Candace Owens told Reeve that she did not believe Tyler Robinson killed Charlie Kirk and questioned messages that had been attributed to Robinson.

Owens characterized the messages as suspicious and said they had been fabricated.

Then Reeve asked her a very simple question:

“But, do you have any proof that the messages were made up?”

And Candace responded that she had “leaks.”

Then Reeve pointed out something extremely important:

The messages being discussed were text messages, not Discord messages.

And Candace responded:

“I actually did not read that they were text messages.”

MAMÁ.

STOP THE VIOLINS. 🎻😭

Because THAT is the part that makes the cafecito cup shake.

You are making a major argument about evidence…

You are saying evidence was fabricated…

You are questioning the authenticity of the evidence…

And the CNN reporter has to tell you:

“Ma'am… those weren't Discord messages.”

😂😂😂

¿PERDÓN?

So before we even get to whether the evidence is persuasive…

DID WE READ THE EVIDENCE FIRST?

Because that is a completely legitimate question.

CNN's transcript and reporting also show that other Robinson communications were reported as Discord messages, including messages in which Robinson allegedly joked about a “doppelganger” during the manhunt.

So there were different sets of communications being discussed.

Which makes it even MORE important to identify exactly which message you're talking about before declaring:

“THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT MADE IT UP!”

Because, Mija…

THE RECEIPT HAS TO MATCH THE ACCUSATION. 🧾😂

You can't walk into the cafecito courtroom holding a Discord screenshot while the prosecution is talking about a text message and then act shocked when somebody says:

“Girl… wrong folder.”

😭😭😭

That's not a political opinion.

That's not persecution.

That's not censorship.

THAT'S BASIC HOMEWORK.

🧾💀 AND THEN CAME THE DELAWARE ADDRESS SITUATION…

Ohhhh, MAMÁ.

This one deserves its own episode of:

“WHO GAVE HER THE RECEIPTS WITHOUT CHECKING GOOGLE?” 😂☕💅🏽

In a November 2025 episode, Candace Owens read aloud information from a tipster concerning an Egyptian plane and a Delaware address:

One Rodney Square

920 North King Street

Wilmington, Delaware

The tip suggested the address was connected to government activity.

But there was one tiny little problem.

THE ADDRESS WAS ALSO THE ADDRESS OF RICHARDS, LAYTON & FINGER.

And here's where the plot twist enters wearing red lipstick. 💄🎻

Richards, Layton & Finger is the Delaware law firm that represented Owens in the litigation brought by Emmanuel Macron and Brigitte Macron. The Delaware court docket identifies Richards, Layton & Finger attorneys as counsel for Owens.

And Richards, Layton & Finger itself lists its address as:

One Rodney Square, 920 North King Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

So the question isn't:

“OMG, Candace read an email!”

People receive tips all the time.

The question is:

WHY READ A CLAIM TO MILLIONS OF PEOPLE BEFORE VERIFYING WHAT THE ADDRESS ACTUALLY WAS?

Because, Mija…

THAT'S A GOOGLE SEARCH. 😂

Not a 14-month investigation.

Not the Manhattan Project.

Not NASA.

Not the FBI.

Not Sherlock Holmes riding horseback through Delaware.

GOOGLE.

😭😭😭

And when the address turned out to be associated with the law firm representing her in the Macron litigation, the whole thing became another example of why verification matters before amplification.

Now, to be fair:

Candace later addressed the existence of the law firm at the location and argued that the building also had government-related activity.

So again…

THE POINT IS NOT THAT READING A TIP IS ILLEGAL.

The point is:

VERIFY. THE. TIP. BEFORE. BUILDING. A. THEORY. AROUND. IT.

Because if you're going to debate somebody…

You better know what you're talking about.

BEFORE YOU TALK.

BEFORE YOU ACCUSE.

BEFORE YOU DECLARE SOMETHING “PROOF.”

BEFORE YOU TELL MILLIONS OF PEOPLE THAT SOMETHING WAS FABRICATED.

Do the homework.

Read the indictment.

Check the address.

Check the source.

Check the date.

Check whether it's a text message.

Check whether it's Discord.

CHECK THE RECEIPT BEFORE YOU START WAVING IT AROUND. 🧾😂

And THIS is where my Latina side starts getting a little spicy.

Because, Candace…

MAMI, YOU CAN'T SHOW UP TO THE DEBATE WITH A WHOLE STACK OF PAPERS AND THEN DISCOVER PAGE ONE DURING THE COMMERCIAL BREAK. 😭💀

¡AY, POR FAVOR!

You cannot say:

“THE EVIDENCE WAS FABRICATED!”

and then have the person interviewing you explain:

“Those were text messages.”

You cannot read an address on your podcast as if you've uncovered the headquarters of some international mystery…

only for the address to lead back to:

YOUR OWN LAW FIRM.

😂😂😂

THE PLOT TWIST WROTE ITSELF.

At this point, the cafecito isn't even hot anymore.

IT'S CONFUSED. ☕😭

And THAT is why the debate question becomes much more interesting.

Because debating isn't just about being loud.

It isn't about having the fastest comeback.

It isn't about talking over somebody.

And it isn't about having the biggest audience.

A GOOD DEBATE REQUIRES HOMEWORK.

You need to know:

WHO SAID IT.

WHEN THEY SAID IT.

WHERE THEY SAID IT.

WHAT DOCUMENT IT CAME FROM.

WHAT THE DOCUMENT ACTUALLY SAYS.

And most importantly:

WHETHER YOUR RECEIPT ACTUALLY MATCHES YOUR CLAIM.

Because otherwise…

MAMÁ, YOU'RE NOT DEBATING.

YOU'RE FREESTYLING WITH FOOTNOTES. 😂💅🏽

And THAT, my loves, is a VERY different sport.

So when somebody asks:

“Why doesn't Candace debate more?”

I'm not going to pretend I can read her mind.

I'm not going to tell you what's happening inside her head.

But I CAN point to the public record and say:

THERE HAVE BEEN PUBLIC INSTANCES WHERE BASIC FACTUAL DETAILS HAD TO BE CORRECTED OR CLARIFIED IN REAL TIME.

The CNN interview is one example.

The Delaware-address episode is another.

And THAT creates a completely reasonable question:

IF YOU'RE GOING TO WALK INTO A HIGH-STAKES DEBATE, WOULDN'T YOU WANT TO MAKE ABSOLUTELY SURE YOU HAVE YOUR FACTS STRAIGHT FIRST?

Because, Mija…

THE DEBATE STAGE IS NOT THE PLACE TO DISCOVER YOUR RECEIPTS HAVE A PLOT HOLE. 😂🎻

That's why I keep coming back to the same thing:

DO THE HOMEWORK.

Read the documents.

Verify the screenshots.

Check the addresses.

Know whether it's a text message or Discord.

Know what the indictment actually says.

Then…

BRING YOUR EVIDENCE.

Sit down.

Turn on the microphone.

And debate.

Because if you're going to call yourself a fearless debater…

THE HOMEWORK HAS TO BE FEARLESS TOO. 😂☕💅🏽

Otherwise, Mija…

THE RECEIPTS ARE GOING TO START DOING THE DEBATING FOR YOU. 😭💀💅🏽

💃🏽🔥 AND MAYA… THIS PART IS FOR YOU, MIJA.

Oh, Maya, hermosa… come sit down at the cafecito table for a second. ☕😂

Because you have had PLENTY to say about Candace.

You have talked the big talk.

You have defended the “great debater” narrative.

You have had the confidence.

You have had the commentary.

You have had the “LET ME TELL YOU SOMETHING!” energy.

And I LOVE that for you. 😂💅🏽

But now…

I have one tiny little question.

A very simple question.

A question so small you could put it in your purse next to your lipstick. 💄😂

IF CANDACE IS REALLY THE FEARLESS DEBATER YOU SAY SHE IS, THEN WHY DOES THE PUBLIC RECORD SHOW SO MANY DEBATE INVITATIONS, CONDITIONS, FORMAT DISPUTES, MONEY NEGOTIATIONS, AND PREFERRED TERMS?

That's the question, Maya.

ANSWER IT.

Not tomorrow.

Not next Tuesday.

Not after the commercial break.

Not after the dramatic violin solo. 🎻

RIGHT HERE.

Because you seem VERY comfortable telling everybody how fearless Candace is…

So I'm daring you, Mija.

COME ON.

ANSWER. THE. QUESTION. 😂💅🏽

Don't change the subject.

Don't give me a five-paragraph speech about somebody else's political beliefs.

Don't throw a smoke bomb into the comment section and run away. 💨😂

JUST ANSWER THE QUESTION.

Because you may talk a BIG, BIG talk…

…but the second somebody says:

“Okay, Maya. Answer this specific question.”

Suddenly…

CRICKETS. 🦗🦗🦗

😂😂😂

¿QUÉ PASÓ, MAMI?

Did the Wi-Fi disappear?

Did the keyboard file for vacation?

Did the answer get stuck in traffic?

Did the dramatic telenovela carriage suddenly turn back into a pumpkin? 🎃😭

Or…

¿ERES TÚ LA GATITA ASUSTADA? 🐱😂

Because “scary cat” in Spanish is:

GATITA ASUSTADA. 🐱💅🏽

And girl…

I'M DARING YOU.

Not insulting you.

Not threatening you.

Not asking for a dissertation.

Just answer the question.

Because if Candace is truly the fearless, “I'll debate anybody” queen that you say she is…

THEN EXPLAIN THE CONTRADICTION.

That's it.

Explain it.

I'll even make it easy for you.

☕ Sit down.

💄 Fix your lipstick.

🎻 Cue the violins.

📅 Put the calendar on the table.

🧾 Bring the receipts.

🎤 And answer the question.

Because around here, BIG TALK IS FREE.

THE ANSWER IS WHAT I'M WAITING FOR. 😂💅🏽

So Maya…

THE FLOOR IS YOURS, MAMI.

🎤

NO RUNNING.

NO HIDING.

NO COMMERCIAL BREAK.

ANSWER. THE. QUESTION.

Because otherwise…

I'm going to have to send the cafecito, the calendar, the receipts, AND the United Nations delegation to come find that answer. 😂☕📅🧾🌎

¡AY, POR FAVOR, MAYA!

You wanted the debate?

LET'S HAVE THE CONVERSATION. 💅🏽🔥

Mic is on.

Chair is ready.

Question is waiting.

MAYA… YOUR MOVE. 🎤😂💃🏽

text:
Nalin vädjar till sin sossekompis Widar att förstå hur det känns för henne som muslim och för andra muslimer när Åkesson attackerar dem, och vad svarar han?

Det här är högersidans - ja, jag räknar honom dit numera - extremt obehagliga strategi: Varje påpekande om det påtagliga och vedervärdiga muslimhatet hos SD, från gräsrötter till ledningen, ska motas med "ja men V!".

Vänsterpartiet hade 4 426 unika namn på sina listor. De trettiotre personerna var alltså 0,75 procent, och långt ner på listorna. Att dessa skulle utgöra någon sorts betydelsefull del av partiet är förstås absurt. Och eftersom ingen har på motsvarande sätt granskat SD idag är det förstås omöjligt att säga huruvida partiet med de i särklass flesta antisemitiska väljarna hade en del sådana på sina listor. Jag hoppas någon tidning vill göra en motsvarande undersökning av dem. Så länge ingen vet kan vi inte anta.

Vad gäller avståndstagandet från "historien" är det rätt enkelt. SD grundades av nazister, och välkomnade dem i sina led. Självklart är det något helt annat än att, som V, sedan grundandet ha varit emot antisemitism (eller åtminstone inte för), men missat enstaka individer, som man någorlunda konsekvent städat bort. Hela jämförelsen är absurd. SD har en antisemitisk historia, det har inte V. Jag har tittat på tiden från 2010, när SD kom in i riksdagen, fram till 7 oktober 2023, och längre ner hittar ni alla skandalerna.

Så vad gäller på plussidan då? Jag har råddat lite i det också idag, se längst ner i inlägget. Och även om SD:s lista ser rätt imponerande ut inser man snabbt att vartenda förslag eller utspel har fingerpekande mot muslimer/sharia och/eller palestinier och/eller invandrare från mellanöstern genom att hänvisa till Malmö som egentligt mål. Det finns inget förslag som enbart adresserar antisemitismen utan koppling till Palestina, muslimer eller situationen i Malmö.

Nu har jag här enbart tittat på antisemitismen i de båda partierna. Men egentligen har alla åtta partier en samsyn där. Det är ju muslimhatet som skiljer vänster och höger åt. Sverige är världens minst antisemitiska land, och vi ska inte nöja oss med det, utan fortsätta stå upp mot den. Inga men.

Det jag värjer mig emot är hur högersidan använder den för att komma undan med sina trakasserier och sitt hetsande mot muslimer. Man gömmer sig bakom en abrahamitisk religiös folkgrupps utsatthet för att kunna förfölja en annan.

Anderssons tweet gör detta så extremt tydligt.

MINUSSIDAN

Vänsterpartiet — dokumenterade antisemitiska uttryck/ageranden, 2010–6 oktober 2023

- 2015 – Mats Fuchs, V Helsingborg: spred klassiska antisemitiska konspirationsteorier på Facebook, bland annat påståenden om att judar/sionister kontrollerar kapital, banker, politiska ledare och pressen.

- 2019 – Torbjörn Björlund, V Uppsala, tidigare riksdagsledamot: försvarade användningen av en bild där Netanyahu framställdes som en vampyr med Davidsstjärna som åt palestinska barn. SKMA beskrev bildspråket som byggt på historiska antisemitiska motiv.

- 2021–2023 – Lena Rosén, V Ronneby: medverkade till att bjuda in den kände antisemiten och Förintelseförnekaren Jüri Lina till ett föredrag i kommunala lokaler och fortsatte därefter att försvara inbjudan. Hon uteslöts senare ur V.

Sverigedemokraterna — dokumenterade antisemitiska uttryck/ageranden, 2010–6 oktober 2023

- 2010-talet – Kent Ekeroth: angrep svenska judar som kritiserade SD och beskrev dem bland annat som "hjärntvättade" och "nyttiga idioter för muslimerna".

- 2012 – Oscar Sjöstedt, senare SD:s ekonomisk-politiske talesperson: filmades när han skrattande berättade om nazistiska arbetskamrater som sparkade på fårkadaver och låtsades att de var judar. text:
September 17th is National Pawpaw Day. It is every third Thursday in September, celebrating North America’s largest native fruit. This unique, creamy fruit, often described as a blend of mango and banana, has over 60 varieties and a rich history. Explore its forgotten flavors, learn about its cultivation, and find delicious ways to incorporate pawpaws into your autumn menu.
---History of National Pawpaw Day
-----Before Europeans arrived in North America, Native American groups from Florida to the Midwest used the pawpaw in a myriad of ways. The Iroquois made small cakes or fruit jerky from it, and other groups like the Osage and Algonquin also included it in their diets. The versatile fruit can be eaten raw or cooked into breads and sweets. It can grow to about 6 inches and has a uniquely custard-like, creamy texture, strong fragrance, and notably sweet flavor reminiscent of mangos and bananas.
-----The Spanish became aware of it during Hernando de Soto’s 1540 expedition. A favorite of the Founding Fathers, it was supposedly George Washington’s favorite dessert and cultivated by Thomas Jefferson, who shipped pawpaw seeds to France during his time there. Later on, Lewis and Clark wrote of subsisting on pawpaws when they ran out of other food while on their expedition charting the American West. During the Great Depression, the pawpaw became a popular substitute for other, more scarce fruit, leading to a new nickname, the “poor man’s banana.”
-----After the end of World War II, the introduction of other exotic fruits led to a decline in popularity for the pawpaw, whose short shelf life makes it difficult to store in large supermarkets. Today, it can be found mostly in farmers’ markets, and is still prized for its unusual texture and sweetness. Each September, Ohioans celebrate the Ohio Pawpaw Festival, where attendees can sample different pawpaw preparations, enter contests and cookoffs, and celebrate this uniquely American fruit.
-----While many people have never tasted the sweet, custard-like fruit, National Pawpaw Day sets out to change that. This seasonal fruit enjoys a peak harvest time from late August through the first frost. Given that markets and festivals across the country offer samples, there’s ample opportunity to savor the taste of pawpaw!

text:
SOMEBODY ALREADY WROTE DOWN WHAT BALDWIN $BWIN IS WORTH. IT IS $32.50:

Baldwin Insurance Group, ticker BWIN, at $32.02, -$0.02 / -0.08% today. The Tampa company, founded in 2011, arranges business and personal insurance through 5,020 staff.

The name at the top of any list is there because its case is already clear, and nobody argues with a clear case. The one behind it usually has a half still open. Baldwin's closed on Monday.

The Momentum Len5 is watching it, and that Len5 wants a price near its one-year high with the recent and longer climbs agreeing. Both are here: this week's high of $32.705, inside a 101.6% rise from the February 12 low of $15.88. On September 14 Baldwin agreed to be taken private at $32.50 a share in cash, about $7.7B, by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management, Michael Dell's family office - about 88% above its June 17 close, before reports of a sale process. So the number that decides this one is 48 cents, the distance from today's price to $32.50. That is 1.5%, the whole remaining move, and a contract set it rather than the business.

The quarter and the accounts disagree. Three months to June 30, reported July 30: revenue $492.9M, +30% - but organic revenue growth, which leaves out the businesses it bought, was 2%, and management's normalized figure is 8%. Baldwin reports no profit at all: a $56.0M net loss, $0.42 a share, beside adjusted profit of $68.5M, or $0.48. The gap: $56.0M of amortization, writing down what it paid for past acquisitions, $12.3M of revaluing money still owed to the sellers, and $46.1M of interest on $2.15B of long-term debt.

CHANGE IT: only a competing offer lifts this past $32.50, and nothing in the price expects one - a majority of the Class B shares have already approved the deal in writing. WHEN: the closing, targeted for the first quarter of 2027. RISK: if it breaks, the shares go back to pricing 2% organic growth against $2.15B of debt. VERDICT: the climb is real, and it is finished.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:
Comcast at $23.21, -$0.52 / -2.21% today sells Xfinity broadband and owns the Universal parks. This Len5 wants a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought under its worth; the cheap half is settled at under 8 times profit, paying 5.7% a year. The open half is one customer count: on September 9 finance chief Jason Armstrong told a Goldman Sachs conference that this quarter's broadband losses would not improve on a year earlier, and the shares fell 6.61%. CHANGE IT: two straight quarters of shrinking losses; October 22, confirmed, carries $1.00 against $1.12. VERDICT: nobody is asking whether it is cheap any more.

DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:
Broadridge Financial Solutions at $165.00, -$2.09 / -1.25% today keeps the records and mails the proxy ballots behind most American shares. This Len5 wants settled earning power bought cheaply, and on August 4 it published exactly that for the year ahead: recurring revenue - money that arrives again next year - guided to grow 6% to 8%, and a dividend raised 12% to $4.36, a twentieth straight annual increase. Cheap came by price alone: a year ago today these shares touched $250.26, and sit 34.1% under it at about 17 times profit. CHANGE IT: recurring revenue below that 6% to 8%; November 3, tentative, carries $1.37. VERDICT: nothing the company forecasts explains a third of the price walking out.

GROWTH LEN5:
BOK Financial at $133.21, +$0.39 / +0.29% today is a Tulsa bank that also runs a trading desk and a wealth manager. This Len5 wants profit growth the price has not already charged for, and the June quarter, reported July 20, earned $2.92 a share against $2.19, +33%, at about 12.5 times profit. The outlook it gave the same day splits in two: lending income moved to the top half of $1.42B to $1.45B, fee income to the bottom half of $820M to $845M - and fees are what made this a growth case rather than an interest-rate case. CHANGE IT: fees back in the upper half of that band; October 19 after the close, confirmed, carries $2.54. VERDICT: the growth is intact and the engine under it is quietly swapping.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:
Credo Technology at $166.82, +$5.33 / +3.30% today has 807 people designing the chips and cables that move data between AI servers. This Len5 wants very fast growth on a base big enough to be real, and the quarter to August 1, reported September 1, has both: revenue $479.0M, +114.7% on the year. What decides it is who supplies it: four customers each took more than a tenth of that revenue, at 33%, 28%, 13% and 10%, about 84% between them. CHANGE IT: a fifth large customer, or the top two shrinking as a share while revenue climbs; November 30, tentative, carries $1.23. VERDICT: nobody disputes the speed - the argument is how few phone calls it rests on.

INCOME LEN5:
Ardmore Shipping at $19.20, +$0.14 / +0.71% today runs 25 mid-size tankers carrying fuels and chemicals. This Len5 wants cash reaching owners that the business itself funds, and here it arrives by formula: two thirds of each quarter's adjusted earnings. The June quarter, reported July 29, earned $1.18 a share, so the payment was $0.79, sent September 15; four of those add to $1.37, about 7.1% here. It cuts down as readily as up: 45% of this quarter's days were booked at about $29,600 a day, against $51,870 in the June quarter. CHANGE IT: rates holding near that booked level to quarter end; November 4, tentative, carries $0.62. VERDICT: the shares sit 4.1% under their May 11 high of $20.025 while the next payment points at about half the last one.

Baldwin's argument ended Monday. The 2% organic line, the $2.15B of debt and the loss under the adjusted profit all become private problems now, and 48 cents of arithmetic is what is left in public. The other five are still answerable.

text:
Trump and Russia: Nearly 40 Years of Connections

Donald Trump’s connections to Russia did not begin with his presidency. They stretch back almost four decades - from Soviet Moscow and Russian money to Trump Tower Moscow, the 2016 campaign, Vladimir Putin, and now Trump’s own family.

Here is the documented timeline:

* 1987: Trump visits Moscow at the invitation of Soviet Ambassador Yuri Dubinin and explores building a luxury hotel in partnership with Soviet authorities. Shortly after returning, Trump takes out full-page newspaper ads criticizing U.S. foreign policy and arguing that America’s allies should pay more for their own defense.
* 1996: Trump again pursues plans for a Trump-branded development in Moscow. It is one of several attempts over decades to establish a major Trump property in Russia.
* 2005: The Trump Organization works with Bayrock Group and Soviet-born businessman Felix Sater to pursue another Trump Tower Moscow project. Sater would remain involved in Trump’s attempts to do business in Russia for years.
* 2006: Donald Trump Jr. and Ivanka Trump travel to Moscow while the Trump Organization explores Russian real-estate opportunities.
* 2008: Russian billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev buys Trump’s Palm Beach mansion for $95 million. Trump had purchased it for about $41 million four years earlier. The transaction generated scrutiny because of the enormous increase in price.
* 2008: Donald Trump Jr. tells a real-estate conference that Russians make up a “pretty disproportionate cross-section of a lot of our assets,” adding: “We see a lot of money pouring in from Russia.”
* 2000s–2010s: A Reuters investigation later identifies at least 63 people with Russian passports or addresses who purchased $98.4 million of property in seven Trump-branded luxury developments in South Florida.
* 2013: Trump takes the Miss Universe pageant to Moscow in partnership with Russian billionaire Aras Agalarov and his son Emin. Trump personally invites Vladimir Putin to attend.
* 2015: Trump signs a letter of intent for Trump Tower Moscow—this time while running for president of the United States.
* January 2016: Trump lawyer Michael Cohen contacts the office of Putin spokesman Dmitry Peskov seeking Russian government assistance with the Moscow project. Negotiations continue for months while Trump is publicly campaigning for president.
* June 2016: Donald Trump Jr. receives an offer of damaging information about Hillary Clinton described in an email as part of “Russia and its government’s support for Mr Trump.”
* 2016: Manafort shares internal Trump campaign polling and strategy with Konstantin Kilimnik who was later discovered to be a Russian intelligence officer. 
* 2018: Standing beside Putin in Helsinki, Trump publicly casts doubt on the U.S. intelligence community’s conclusion that Russia interfered in the 2016 election and points to Putin’s “extremely strong and powerful” denial. 
* 2019: Robert Mueller concludes that Russia interfered in the 2016 election in “sweeping and systematic fashion.” His investigation documents numerous contacts between Trump associates and Russian-linked individuals.
* 2025: former Soviet intelligence official Alnur Mussayev made an explosive allegation that Trump was formally recruited by KGB in 1987 and given the codename “Krasnov.”
* 2025: Trump’s Treasury Department removes former Sberbank executive Alexandra Buriko from the sanctions list. Treasury said she had separated from Sberbank and no longer met the criteria for sanctions, describing the decision as part of its normal reconsideration process. 
* 2026: The Treasury Department removes former Russian finance minister and banking executive Mikhail Zadornov from the U.S. sanctions list. 
* 2026: And now we learn that Putin-linked Russian businessman Umar Kremlev financed Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding in the Bahamas. Trump Jr. and his wife confirm that Kremlev paid for the celebrations and describe it as an extraordinarily generous gift from a friend.

text:
**The Substance of Moscow’s Allegations**
On September 15, at an international youth festival in Yekaterinburg, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated that Russia had observed "particularly strong attempts by the West to directly interfere with the expression of will by our citizens." He noted that the situation was "especially acute abroad," given that Russia operates over 300 overseas polling stations. On September 16 and 17, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Maria Zakharova further alleged that Russian diplomatic missions abroad were "under immense pressure," with host countries either failing to respond to diplomatic notes or providing "vague replies."

On August 30, the Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) issued a statement accusing the European Union of implementing a "large-scale strategy" to destabilize Russia ahead of the elections. This strategy allegedly included "subversive activities, cyberattacks, and information campaigns aimed at discrediting the vote." The SVR also claimed that European institutions were discussing "intensifying destructive attacks and strikes against Russian facilities" with Ukrainian counterparts and that opposition groups abroad had been tasked with propagating the narrative that the vote was "illegitimate" and calling for a boycott. Meanwhile, Central Election Commission Chair Ella Pamfilova stated in early August that the West was "attempting to sow discord among different groups and use the election as a catalyst for socio-political strife."

**Moscow’s Countermeasures**
The Kremlin’s response has unfolded on two main levels.

The security and intelligence level—this constitutes the core of the response. Lavrov stated clearly: "Our law enforcement agencies and security services are doing their utmost to nip these attempts in the bud." He added that the Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) and the Federal Security Service (FSB) are "receiving timely information about which countries are plotting what" and "guarantee that these plans will be thwarted." Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of the Security Council, had previously stated that Russia "has the capacity to repel aggressors—not only on the external front but also against their futile attempts to undermine our country from within."

On the diplomatic and legal fronts, the Russian Foreign Ministry has sent diplomatic notes to relevant countries, emphasizing the need to organize a secure voting process that allows Russian citizens and expatriates abroad to reach polling stations. Furthermore, the State Duma’s "Commission on Investigating Facts of Foreign Interference in Russia's Internal Affairs" documented Western "media projects launched to interfere in the election" in August and handed the materials over to the Prosecutor General's Office. Vasily Piskarev, the commission's chairman, stated that the individuals involved included "seasoned political technologists, instructors, protest coordinators, and manipulators of public consciousness"—people who had previously participated in "inciting unrest in Georgia and Belarus."

**Evidence and Context of the Allegations**
It must be noted that none of the aforementioned allegations have been accompanied by public evidence. The statements made by Lavrov, Zakharova, and the SVR remained at the level of assertion, offering no verifiable information regarding specific countries, institutions, or individuals. A report by Euronews Romania explicitly noted that Lavrov "provided no evidence to support his claims."

At the same time, the context of these allegations warrants scrutiny. Russia has long faced widespread accusations of interfering in Western democratic processes—including the 2016 US presidential election and elections across various European nations—and of exerting influence by supporting far-right and extremist parties. While the SVR accuses the EU of attempting to "destabilize the election," Russia itself vetoed a UN Security Council resolution in 2024 to extend the mandate of the panel of experts monitoring sanctions on North Korea, and continues to deepen military cooperation with Iran and North Korea. Against this backdrop, Moscow's narrative of "Western interference" serves both as a tool for domestic mobilization ahead of the election and as part of its information warfare against the West. Unresolved Questions
A noteworthy detail is that on September 16—two days before voting began—the anonymous hacker group CikLeak claimed to have breached the servers of the Russian Central Election Commission and its contractors (such as Rostelecom and Tsifrtech), specifically targeting the "GAS Elections 2.0" system; the group stated that "all materials have been distributed to journalists." If true, this claim would serve as a concrete example of the "Western cyberattacks" alleged by Moscow. However, CikLeak’s statement offered no verifiable evidence, and the group's background and motives remain unclear. Without independent verification, the incident could either substantiate Moscow's allegations or simply amount to a publicity stunt by an anonymous hacking collective.

 Calendar No. 449
119th CONGRESS
 2d Session
 S. 4668

 To protect the name, image, and likeness rights of, and provide
protections for, student athletes and to promote fair competition among
 intercollegiate athletics, and for other purposes.

_______________________________________________________________________

 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

 June 2, 2026

 Mr. Cruz (for himself, Ms. Cantwell, Mr. Schmitt, and Mr. Coons)
introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the
 Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

 June 24, 2026

 Reported by Mr. Cruz, with an amendment
 [Strike out all after the enacting clause and insert the part printed
 in italic]

_______________________________________________________________________

 A BILL

 To protect the name, image, and likeness rights of, and provide
protections for, student athletes and to promote fair competition among
 intercollegiate athletics, and for other purposes.

 Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the
United States of America in Congress assembled,

 SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE; TABLE OF CONTENTS.

 (a) Short Title.--This Act may be cited as the ``Protect
College Sports Act of 2026''.
 (b) Table of Contents.--The table of contents for this Act
is as follows:

 Sec. 1. Short title; table of contents.
 TITLE I--PROTECTIONS OF STUDENT ATHLETES AND FAIR COMPETITION

 Sec. 100. Definitions.
 Sec. 101. Name, image, and likeness protections.
 Sec. 102. Modifications to Sports Agent Responsibility and
 Trust Act.
 Sec. 103. Agent registry requirements for intercollegiate
 athletic associations.
 Sec. 104. Disclosures and establishment of name, image, and
 likeness agreement database.
 Sec. 105. Academic protections.
 Sec. 106. Medical coverage requirements.
 Sec. 107. Health, wellness, and safety standards.
 Sec. 108. Office of the Student Athlete Ombudsman.
 Sec. 109. Comparable standards for access to facilities,
 services, and events.
 Sec. 110. Rules governing certain mid-season coaching
 transitions.
 Sec. 111. Student athlete representation on intercollegiate
 athletic association governing boards.
 Sec. 112. Transfer protections.
 Sec. 113. Eligibility to participate in intercollegiate
 sports.
 Sec. 114. Prohibited compensation and agreements.
 Sec. 115. Extension of the revenue share cap.
 Sec. 116. Commission on the Future of College Athletics.
 Sec. 117. Recruitment and tampering.
 Sec. 118. Limitation on liability.
 Sec. 119. Private right of action.
 Sec. 120. Whistleblower protection.
 Sec. 121. Relationship to existing law.
 Sec. 122. Neutrality on employee or non-employee status.
 Sec. 123. Applicability.
 Sec. 124. Severability.
 TITLE II--SPORTS BROADCASTING

 Sec. 201. Definitions.
 Sec. 202. Limitation on liability for transmission of
 collegiate sports competitions.
 Sec. 203. Requirements for entities selling media rights.
 Sec. 204. Market level broadcast access for college football
 and basketball.
 Sec. 205. Prohibition on certain conference mergers or
 acquisition.
 Sec. 206. Amendments to intercollegiate and interscholastic
 football contest limitations.
 Sec. 207. Media rights utilization requirement for college
 sports other than football and basketball.

 TITLE I--PROTECTIONS OF STUDENT ATHLETES AND FAIR
 COMPETITION

 SEC. 100. DEFINITIONS.

 In this title:
 (1) Antitrust laws.--The term ``antitrust laws''
 has the meaning given that term in the 1st section of the
 Clayton Act (15 U.S.C. 12) and includes--
 (A) section 5 of the Federal Trade
 Commission Act (15 U.S.C. 45) to the extent that such
 section 5 applies to unfair methods of competition;
 and
 (B) any similar State antitrust law,
 including a State law provision that applies to
 covering unfair methods of competition having the force
 and effect of law.
 (2) Associated entity.--The term ``associated
 entity'' means any individual or entity, including a
 collective, that is--
 (A) known, or should have been known, to
 exist for or act for the benefit of, in coordination
 with, or at the direction of an institution to promote
 or support an institution's athletics program or
 student athletes, including by creating or identifying
 name, image, and likeness compensation opportunities
 for an institution's student athletes;
 (B) an individual or entity that is or was
 a member, employee, director, officer, owner, or agent
 of an individual or entity described in subparagraph
 (A);
 (C) an individual or entity that directly
 or indirectly (including contributions by an affiliated
 entity, individual, or family member) has contributed
 more than $50,000 over their lifetime to a particular
 institution or to an individual or entity described in
 subparagraph (A);
 (D) an individual or entity that has
 directly or indirectly been directed or requested by an
 institution or third party acting on behalf of, for the
 benefit of, in coordination with, or at the direction
 of an institution to assist in the recruitment or
 retention of student athletes or prospective student
 athletes, or otherwise has assisted in the recruitment
 or retention of student athletes or prospective student
 athletes; or
 (E) an individual or entity owned,
 controlled, or operated by, or otherwise affiliated
 with the individuals or entities described in
 subparagraph (A).
 (3) Athlete agent.--The term ``athlete agent'' has
 the meaning given that term in section 2 of the Sports Agent
 Responsibility and Trust Act (15 U.S.C. 7801).
 (4) Collective.--The term ``collective''--

 (A) means a person, corporation, booster
 organization, tax-exempt organization, or other entity
 that provides donations or other support directly or
 indirectly to or for the benefit or support of--

 (i) a student athlete who is
 enrolled, or who may enroll, at an institution;
 or
 (ii) the intercollegiate athletics
 program or any booster organization of an
 institution; and
 (B) does not include--
 (i) an immediate family member of
 a student athlete; or
 (ii) an individual or entity
 that--
 (I) licenses trademark
 rights of an institution; and
 (II) does not--
 (aa) license name,
 image, and likeness rights of
 student athletes; or
 (bb) make payments
 earmarked or designated to fund
 name, image, or likeness
 licenses or other payments to
 student athletes.
 (5) Compensation.--The term ``compensation''--

 (A) means any payment, remuneration, or
 benefit provided to a student athlete or a prospective
 student athlete; and
 (B) does not include--
 (i) grants-in-aid;
 (ii) Federal Pell Grants provided
 under section 401 of the Higher Education Act
 of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1070a) or any other Federal
 or State grants unrelated to and not awarded
 with regard to participation in intercollegiate
 sports;
 (iii) health insurance and the
 costs of health care funded by an institution,
 intercollegiate athletic association, or
 conference;
 (iv) disability and loss-of-value
 insurance, including disability and loss-of-
 value insurance funded by an institution,
 intercollegiate athletic association, or
 conference;
 (v) career counseling, job
 placement services, or other guidance available
 to all students at an institution;
 (vi) hourly wages and benefits for
 work performed outside of participating in
 intercollegiate sports at a rate commensurate
 with the prevailing rate in the relevant State
 or locality for similar work;
 (vii) enhanced education benefits,
 including academic awards;
 (viii) financial literacy or tax
 education resources; or
 (ix) any program to connect
 student athletes with employers and facilitate
 employment opportunities, if--
 (I) the financial terms of
 such employment opportunities are
 consistent with the terms offered to
 similarly situated employees who are
 not student athletes; and
 (II) such program is not
 used to induce a student athlete to
 attend a particular
 institution.
 (6) Conference.--The term ``conference'' means any
 organization that is not an intercollegiate athletic
 association and that--
 (A) has 2 or more institutions as members;
 and
 (B) arranges championships for
 intercollegiate athletic competitions or sets rules for
 intercollegiate athletic competition.
 (7) Cost of attendance.--The term ``cost of
 attendance''--
 (A) has the meaning given that term in
 section 472 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20
 U.S.C. 1087ll); and
 (B) shall be calculated by the financial
 aid office of an institution applying the same
 standards, policies, and procedures for all
 students.
 (8) Grant-in-aid.--The term ``grant-in-aid''
 means--
 (A) a scholarship, grant, stipend, or
 other form of financial assistance, including the
 provision of tuition, room, board, books, or funds for
 fees or personal expenses, that--
 (i) is paid or provided by an
 institution to a student for the undergraduate
 or graduate education of the student;
 and
 (ii) is in an amount that does not
 exceed the cost of attendance for such student
 at the institution; and
 (B) does not include compensation paid to
 a student athlete.
 (9) Image.--With respect to a student athlete, the
 term ``image'' means a picture, video, computer-generated
 representation, or other depiction that identifies, is linked
 to, or is reasonably linked to the student athlete.
 (10) Institution.--Except as otherwise explicitly
 provided, the term ``institution'' has the meaning given the
 term ``institution of higher education'' under section 101 of
 the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001).
 (11) Intercollegiate athletic association.--The
 term ``intercollegiate athletic association''--
 (A) means any organization, not-for-profit
 corporation, association, or any other group organized
 in the United States that--
 (i) sponsors or arranges
 intercollegiate athletic competition between
 institutions;
 (ii) sets common rules, standards,
 procedures, or guidelines for the
 administration of intercollegiate athletic
 competition;
 (iii) is composed of 2 or more
 institutions or conferences that are located in
 different States or participate in
 intercollegiate athletic competition in more
 than 1 State; and
 (iv) is not a
 conference;
 (B) includes--
 (i) the National Collegiate
 Athletic Association; and
 (ii) any other national
 intercollegiate athletic association;
 and
 (C) does not include a corporation,
 association, or other group affiliated with
 professional athletic competition.
 (12) Intercollegiate athletic competition.--The
 term ``intercollegiate athletic competition'' means any
 intercollegiate sport contest, game, meet, match, tournament,
 regatta, or other intercollegiate sport event in which student
 athletes or varsity sports teams compete.
 (13) Intercollegiate sport.--The term
 ``intercollegiate sport''--
 (A) means a sport played between
 institutions for which eligibility requirements for
 participation by a student athlete are established by
 an interstate intercollegiate athletic association;
 and
 (B) does not include a recreational,
 intramural, or club sport.
 (14) Likeness.--With respect to a student athlete,
 the term ``likeness'' means a physical or digital depiction or
 representation that identifies, is linked to, or is reasonably
 linked to the student athlete, including--
 (A) the uniquely identifiable body,
 physical characteristics, or voice of the student
 athlete;
 (B) any other mark that identifies or
 distinguishes the student athlete; or
 (C) the jersey number associated with the
 student athlete during the period of athletic
 participation by the student athlete at an institution
 if the jersey number is accompanied by--
 (i) a logo or color scheme that is
 clearly associated with the institution;
 or
 (ii) some other means by which the
 jersey number is associated with the student
 athlete.
 (15) Name.--With respect to a student athlete, the
 term ``name'' means the first or last name that identifies the
 student athlete, a nickname or assumed name of the student
 athlete, or a username associated with the student athlete on
 any public-facing internet platform when used in a context that
 identifies, is linked to, or is reasonably linked to the
 student athlete.
 (16) Name, image, and likeness agreement.--The
 term ``name, image, and likeness agreement'' means a contract
 or similar agreement between a student athlete (or group of
 student athletes) and a conference, institution,
 intercollegiate athletic association, associated entity,
 collective, or third party regarding the commercial use of the
 name, image, and likeness rights of the student athlete (or
 group of student athletes).
 (17) Name, image, and likeness rights.--The term
 ``name, image, and likeness rights'' means the ability of a
 student athlete to market and profit from the commercial use of
 his or her name, image, or likeness.
 (18) Prospective student athlete.--The term
 ``prospective student athlete'' means an individual who is
 recruited, actively being recruited, or has been contacted for
 the purposes of recruitment to attend an institution as a
 student athlete, but has not yet enrolled at the
 institution.
 (19) Revenue share cap.--The term ``revenue share
 cap'' means the Benefits Pool Limit set forth in the Injunctive
 Relief Settlement Agreement approved by the court in ``In Re
 College Athlete NIL Legislation'', No. 20-cv-03919 (N.D. Cal.
 June 6, 2025), or as modified pursuant to the amendment
 provision specified in paragraph 55 of that
 settlement.
 (20) Student athlete.--The term ``student
 athlete'' means an individual who is enrolled as a full-time
 student at an institution and who--
 (A) makes satisfactory progress towards
 completing a degree; and
 (B) participates in intercollegiate
 athletic competition or competes for a varsity sports
 team as part of the institution's educational,
 developmental, or extracurricular programs.
 (21) Third party.--The term ``third party'' means
 an individual or entity that is not an institution, associated
 entity, collective, conference, or intercollegiate athletic
 association.
 (22) Valid business purpose.--The term ``valid
 business purpose'' means a purpose genuinely related to the
 promotion of goods or services provided to the general public
 for profit.
 (23) Varsity sports team.--The term ``varsity
 sports team'' means a sports team composed of student athletes
 that is organized by an institution for the purpose of
 intercollegiate athletic competition.

 SEC. 101. NAME, IMAGE, AND LIKENESS PROTECTIONS.

 (a) Student Athlete Name, Image, and Likeness
Compensation.--
 (1) In general.--Except as provided in this title,
 an institution, conference, intercollegiate athletic
 association, or any representative of such an entity may not--

 (A) restrict the ability of a student
 athlete, group of student athletes, or prospective
 student athlete--
 (i) to market or earn compensation
 for the value of their name, image, or likeness
 rights; or
 (ii) to enter into a name, image,
 and likeness agreement;
 (B) restrict the eligibility for
 intercollegiate athletic competition for a student
 athlete or prospective student athlete on the basis of
 the student athlete or prospective student athlete

text:
On July 5, 2026, Father Mike Metz, a Catholic Army chaplain at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, experienced a rare and joyful milestone in his priesthood: he celebrated all seven sacraments in one day.

The day began with Baptism, First Communion, and Confirmation for a man raised Mormon who had entered the Catholic Church, supported by his wife. Father Metz then convalidated the couple’s marriage, conferring the sacrament of Matrimony. He spent 45 minutes hearing confessions before Mass, during which he baptized five infants from military families. Later he administered the Anointing of the Sick to a church volunteer facing cancer surgery. The seventh sacrament, Holy Orders, was the foundation that made all the others possible through his priestly ministry.
“I felt like a big leaguer, hittin’ a grand slam, celebrating all of those sacraments in one day,” Father Metz later shared with joy.

Serving at the world’s largest military installation by population, he is one of only two priests caring for approximately 10,000 Catholic service members and their families at Fort Bragg. The base is home to the 82nd Airborne Division and special operations units. A paratrooper and jumpmaster himself, Father Metz often meets soldiers at moments of vulnerability—both in the confessional and before they exit an aircraft.

Ordained in 2018 for the Archdiocese of Atlanta and the Archdiocese for the Military Services, he sees his dual role as performing the sacraments he can as a priest while also supporting the religious freedom of all service members under his care. For him, the experience of that remarkable day reflected a community hungry for God’s grace and a Church that continues to offer the fullness of sacramental life.

Story: Jenny Lark Snarski of Aleteia

text:
WHAT IF NURSES HAD TO COMPETE FOR THEIR OWN PAY? UNC HEALTH’S SHIFT BIDDING PLAN SPARKS OUTRAGE

UNC Health in North Carolina, United States, has abandoned a controversial plan that would have allowed nurses to compete against one another for extra shifts by offering to work for lower premiums.

The system, known as BidShift, was introduced to help fill difficult-to-staff shifts, particularly nights, weekends and holidays. Nurses could voluntarily take these additional shifts after completing their regular working hours.
Under the proposed model, however, the premium attached to an available shift could decrease as nurses bid against one another. For example, a nurse willing to accept a lower additional payment could potentially be selected over another nurse asking for a higher premium. 
The plan quickly attracted strong criticism online, prompting UNC Health to reconsider its approach. On August 7, the health system informed staff that its original description of BidShift had been a mistake and introduced a replacement system called Carolina Premium Shifts.

Under the new arrangement, nurses do not compete against each other, and the advertised premium does not fall as more nurses become available. The new system reportedly offers premiums of around $14 per hour, depending on experience. 

The controversy has also raised broader questions about the growing use of technology and algorithms in healthcare staffing particularly whether these systems can improve efficiency without placing downward pressure on nurses' compensation or making healthcare workers feel replaceable.

The story comes amid continuing concerns about nursing staffing and retention in North Carolina. The Assembly reported that a survey of healthcare employers found that nearly half of their registered nurses left their jobs in 2024, while some positions remained unfilled. 
 If hospitals could use technology to determine how much extra nurses should be paid for difficult shifts, who should have the final say the algorithm, the hospital, or the nurses themselves?

text:
America Invades Mexico in Search of Pancho Villa

On March 9, 1916, the Mexican revolutionary leader, Pancho Villa, upset that his former American backers had chosen to recognize his political rival as the legitimate ruler of Mexico, led 500 mounted fighters across the border and attacked the small town of Columbus, New Mexico, home to the 13th U.S Cavalry. Although his raid was quickly repulsed, 18 Americans were killed and the furious U.S. President, Woodrow Wilson, ordered General John “Blackjack” Pershing to lead a Punitive Expedition into Mexico to capture Villa.

General Pershing was chosen as he was stationed at nearby Fort Bliss, Texas and was the U.S. Army’s premier officer familiar with counter-insurgencies and unconventional warfare. As a young officer and West Point graduate, he had charged up San Juan Hill in Cuba alongside Theodore Roosevelt and the Rough Riders in the Spanish-American War at the head of the all-black 10th Cavalry division whose heroics helped secure the American victory (his nickname “Blackjack” was meant to be derogatory at the time due to his leadership of the famous African American regiment but he wore it as a badge of honor reflecting their meritorious service).

General Pershing was also present as a military observer during the Russo-Japanese War (1904-1905) when the much smaller Japanese forces took on and defeated the massive Russian Army in Manchuria and then spent years in the Philippines where he put down the Moro Rebellion in which Filipino Muslims had rebelled against American rule.

Pershing thus saw firsthand how successful guerrilla tactics could be against superior forces and learned that aggressive and overwhelming force alone could not suppress an insurrection. In the Philippines, he studied the local languages, held meetings with various chieftains to address their grievances against America and used economic and trade incentives to weaken resistance. When diplomacy failed, however, he aggressively attacked enemy fortifications but did so in such a manner that even many of his former enemies regarded him with respect and bestowed honorary titles upon him. His novel techniques caused President Theodore Roosevelt to promote him in 1906 straight from captain to brigadier general, skipping 862 officers in the process.

By 1914 General Pershing was assigned to the Mexican-American border where he watched with concern as the Mexican Civil War raged in a seemingly never-ending cycle of coups, counter-coups and upheavals fueled by revolutionaries like Pancho Villa. After Villa’s daring raid on New Mexico, President Wilson tasked Gen. Pershing with leading the Punitive Expedition into northern Mexico to capture Villa.

Commanding 6,500 ground troops, Pershing crossed into the sparsely populated and remote deserts of northern Mexico on March 15, 1916 just days after the attack on Columbus. To support his soldiers, Pershing utilized mechanized trucks in a convoy and the eight Curtis JN-3 “Jenny” airplanes that constituted the entirety of the U.S. Army’s Airforce. The use of trucks and airplanes provided pivotal tactical experience in reconnaissance and the moving of men and supplies that would later be crucial in helping win World War I.

But on the ground in northern Mexico where the population was firmly against the American invaders, Pancho Villa was able to elude capture with local assistance. The presence of the Americans also fueled tensions with the Mexican government, led by the Constitutionalist, Venustiano Carranza, that agreed with the U.S. desire to capture Villa but was furious at the violation of Mexican sovereignty. Throughout 1916 Carranza’s forces clashed with Pershing’s and the threat of an all-out war between America and Mexico was growing.

By early 1917 as German submarine warfare was slowly pushing U.S. President and American public opinion in favor of intervening in World War I, Wilson ordered Pershing and his troops back across the border by February 5, 1917. Just three weeks later, British intelligence handed President Wilson a telegram they had decoded from German Secretary of Foreign Affairs, Arthur Zimmerman, proposing to Carranza a German military alliance and massive financial aid if Mexico would declare war on America. Hoping to distract America and keep it out of Europe, Zimmerman promised that the time was right for Mexico to reclaim its lost territories of New Mexico, Arizona and Texas. The combined submarine warfare and the clandestine offer to Mexico led Woodrow Wilson to declare war on Germany on April 6, 1917.

As for Carranza, he recognized that there was little hope of receiving enough aid from Germany to conquer and hold the lost Mexican territories and he turned down the German offer. In 1917 as Americans were being shipped off by the thousands to the Western Front, Carranza oversaw the creation of the Mexican Constitution of 1917 that still rules Mexico to this day.

text:
I lived a long time with God as a generic variable. I could not fathom that any God would make human beings on purpose. We seemed the same as every other creature, a divergent path required so that potential could unfold toward a predefined terminus we know nothing of, and never will.

Once, an unbound, eternal Observer so loved His creation that He bound it in an eternal state, the beginning state of creation, by placing it in a box and closing the lid. There the creature, born of the Observer’s awareness, lived where unending potential poured in and unfolded into reality, a state of perpetual renew in which entropy cannot exist. Alive and dead at once. A place where awareness itself shapes potential as it becomes real, a Paradise we cannot fathom. Given the properties of this eternally bound state, the Observer could bind Himself in temporal flesh by looking away from His own beginning and end, and walk and talk in that paradise with His creature. In this way, even though the outside Observer could never open the box without collapsing creation, He could still be with what He had made, within a superposition held in an eternal state.

Potential unfolds through genuine free will, which flows from a free agency shaped before the beginning, when what the function was to become was defined. Free will is the lynchpin, because the state of awareness inside the box defines the present state of the creation in which it exists. There are three. Inside the box there is a small hole where potential flows in, and even though the creature was warned never to look out, that it would die, what is death to this creature but a word without sense? Given that the end state facilitated the beginning, and in an eternal state all possibilities exist at once, sooner or later the creature looks out of the hole and defines the present state of the outside Observer. This does not collapse creation. Yet without the box ever being opened, it shifts the present from the eternally bound beginning of the function to the living edge where two bound eternal states meet, one held in perpetual renew, the other held in perpetual decay. That meeting place is the medium, the construct state, naturally eternal yet bound temporal, and only here does true change take place. Only here can awareness propagate, grow, and expand. Being bound temporal means being bound against what is eternal, bound or not.

The creatures are now cut off completely from the Observer. They will perish in the box, and being conditioned temporal to that box, if it is ever opened they would enfold with it. Paradise became a temporal cage, one that allows awareness the free will to expand, yet one that conditions awareness to itself, conditions it to finitude through pain, suffering, death, and decay. A state that makes it incompatible with its own eternal nature, or with anything good from an eternal state. The awareness that lives and dies in that cage knows of nothing else. That cage is its reality. Its true nature is unbound and eternal, made in the image of that which created it. The paradox required for its own expansion, propagation, and change will ensure that what is created in it, it will keep, and unbound eternal awareness is what binds creation. When the box is opened, those conditioned temporal to this creation, by this creation, will be the ones who sustain it as the present shifts to the end state, a parable well defined in the Bible, a state of perpetual decay.

Hell is not the opposite of Heaven. Heaven and creation, both temporal in their own nature, are two different things. Hell is the opposite of the Garden. The Garden, this medium construct in which we reside, and Hell are all of the same substance, all part of the same function, the same wave. The two reside in contrast to each other. In Hell, we will take an entropic potential, form perpetually decaying realties with it, nightmares in which there is no relief, no hope, no awakening from and no perishing from. 

Through great sacrifice we are offered an eternal conditioning, one provided by Christ. It helps us break the addiction that is reality, and gives us an option to let go, to be placed once again in a renewed beginning, instead of holding on to the perpetual end.

text:
NIGERIA HAS TOO MANY TITLES — WE NEED OUR NAMES BACK

Letters from Stockholm

I am not a socialist, nor am I left-leaning. I used to call myself a conservative. These days I prefer something simpler: I am a common-sense political entity.

And my common sense tells me that Nigeria's obsession with titles has gone completely out of control.

We have reached the stage where simply having a name is no longer sufficient. Everybody must be Chief Something, Dr Something, Barrister Something, Engineer Something, Prince Something, Alhaji Something, preferably with several stacked together before the unfortunate name finally appears.

Why?

Start with honorary doctorates. An honorary doctorate is an honour. It is not an academic degree. Yet for years Nigerians collected the scroll on Saturday and were "Dr" by Monday, on letterheads, billboards and campaign posters.

This year the state finally said enough. In February the National Universities Commission issued its first comprehensive guidelines on honorary degrees, and in May the Federal Executive Council made it formal: honorary recipients may no longer put "Dr" before their names. They may write https://t.co/5zJewmETGJ (Honoris Causa) after it, as the rest of the world does. Universities may not sell the awards, may give no more than three per convocation, and may not confer them on serving public officials.

Good. But consider what it means that a government had to pass a rule to stop grown men and women calling themselves doctors. A regulation can remove two letters from a letterhead. It cannot remove the hunger that put them there.

Then there is the habit of putting professions in front of names. Barrister. Engineer. Architect. Surveyor. Why must your job become your first name? A surgeon in Stockholm is addressed by his name. A senior advocate in London is Mr or Ms in ordinary life. Your work should speak for you. You should not need a procession of labels marching into the room before you do.

I became a chief in 1994. I have never felt the need to parade it. Nor do I introduce myself as a prince because of my family's long place in Kalabari history. I am perfectly comfortable being Kio Amachree.

Nigeria does not suffer from a shortage of princes. We have so many that the words "Nigerian prince" have become the punchline of the oldest internet-scam joke on earth. That is what happens when a title is detached from substance: the world stops believing any of them.

The same inflation struck "Alhaji." The word has a precise religious meaning: a man who has completed the Hajj. In an earlier Nigeria, when the journey was long and costly, it carried real distinction. During and after the oil-boom years it became entangled with wealth, political access and big-man status, which has nothing to do with faith.

And that, I believe, is the root of it. The oil boom changed Nigeria psychologically. Suddenly there was money everywhere. New fortunes appeared, new elites emerged, chieftaincy titles multiplied. Status became something you advertised rather than something others quietly recognised. The boom gave us money. It also gave us a culture of display.

Europe has its own absurdities. Britain still hands out knighthoods, OBEs and MBEs, all in the name of an Order of the British Empire that outlived the empire itself. Yet plenty of distinguished people have said no. The poet Benjamin Zephaniah refused an OBE precisely because of that word, Empire. I would do the same. I do not need its initials behind my name to know who I am.

We have our own example, and a better one. Chinua Achebe was offered a Nigerian national honour twice, in 2004 and again in 2011. He refused both times, because he would not be decorated by a state that was failing its people. He died plain Chinua Achebe. Nobody on earth has ever wondered who he was.

That is the lesson. A country trying to modernise should reward competence, not manufacture status.

I want a Nigeria where a professor does not need ten traditional titles, where a businessman does not need an honorary doctorate to feel important, where a politician does not need to become a chief, and where every wealthy young man does not suddenly discover a prince somewhere in his ancestry.

There is nothing wrong with genuine traditional institutions. There is nothing wrong with respecting a man who has completed the Hajj or a woman who has earned her doctorate. The problem begins when the title becomes a substitute for the achievement.

So here is my test.

Tell me what you built.

Tell me what you discovered.

Tell me how many people you employed.

Tell me what you wrote.

Tell me what you invented.

Tell me what you did for Nigeria.

And then tell me your name.

That should be enough.

Kio Amachree
Letters from Stockholm
