text:
Why do you do this James? You’re grasping at straws. 

Let’s examine the purpose of the mosaic law. 

The civil laws given in Deuteronomy including penalties like stoning for adultery, Sabbath-breaking, or rebellion were not given as universal laws for all nations and all time.
Israel was uniquely constituted as a nation governed directly by God (a theocracy). The civil code was designed to maintain national, ritual, and moral purity within that specific geopolitical covenantal community.
The severe penalties of the Mosaic Law served to demonstrate the absolute holiness of God, the gravity of sin, and the absolute standards of a righteous society. However, they functioned within the temporary framework of the Old Covenant.
God deals with humanity progressively through history. God instituted specific civil statutes for Israel that pointed forward to a greater reality.

Jesus did not "ignore" or arbitrarily give permission to break the law; rather, He fulfilled it. In Matthew 5:17–18, Jesus explicitly stated:"Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I have not come to abolish them but to fulfill them. For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth disappear, not the smallest letter, not the least stroke of a pen, will by any means disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished."  
What "Fulfillment" Means? In biblical theology, Jesus fulfilled the law by living a perfectly sinless life under it, by embodying its ultimate moral intent, and by bearing the ultimate penalty of the law on the cross. Because He accomplished everything the law pointed toward, the old covenant administrative and civil structures reached their completion.

When challenged about specific civil or judicial penalties from the Mosaic Law, Jesus consistently redirected hearts to the underlying moral reality and demonstrated how the New Covenant operates. 

Consider this: When religious leaders brought a woman caught in the act of adultery to Jesus. Jesus did not abolish the moral reality that adultery is sin. Instead, He exposed the hypocrisy of her accusers ("Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her") and offered both justice and grace: "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more." Jesus upheld the moral law while transcending the temporary penal code of theocratic Israel.

Jesus taught that the entire Law and the Prophets hang on two ultimate moral commands. Those are loving God and loving one's neighbor (Matthew 22:37–40)

Christians do not claim that "every word" of the Bible such as ancient civil penalties, dietary restrictions, or temple rituals is binding as a civil law today. The Apostle Paul clarifies this in Romans 10:4: "Christ is the culmination of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes." We live under the New Covenant, where the eternal moral character of God remains unchanging, but the temporary civil statutes of ancient Israel have achieved their purpose in Christ.

text:
I don't think the tokenization story is well understood - so let's break it down 

Basically - the US Government is in vast, unprecedented amount of debt. And its long term debt is selling off a lot (40%+ over 5 years) - while Gold is up 140%. Gold has crossed US treasuries as the #1 asset held by other Central Banks. 

The buyers for US debt - China, Japan and Europe are stepping away for different reasons. Geopolitical conflict. Currency related. Political difference. 

The government is afraid of running out of buyers for its debt. And it's worried about the liquidity of markets. Historically, this concern is much worse when the Fed is hiking and there's high inflation. As typically the response to unstable debt markets is easing (buying debt). 

Therefore, the US government is very incentivized to allow Stablecoins. Stablecoins hoover up US debt. Tether has different balance sheet behavior than banks and works closely with the US government. 

Stablecoins used to be assumed to be criminal operations and were prosecuted by the USG. Now they're welcomed to Washington DC.  

When you are worried about your reserve currency status, you also want to ensure the dollar is accepted in many places. So stablecoins not only serve as a buyer of US debt, but a promoter of the US dollar globally. 

Enter CBDCs. Europeans see the US government promoting US dollar stablecoins as a matter of foreign policy. Visa and Mastercard going heavy in the space. And see Tether freezing Balances along with the DOJ and say, "We cannot have this. We don't want Trump to be able to use the US dollar in negotiations with us. Therefore we have to digitize our currency" 

Europe and the UK also have fiscal and political problems. So the perverse incentive to digitize their currencies is not just to ensure 'monetary sovereignty' but also to potentially implement wealth taxes, or balance based transaction taxes. This is also the flip side of wide adoption of US dollar stables. We don't call it a CDBC, but its basically an extension of the government. Balances are frequently frozen. Other policies could be implemented under the left.

So rising global debt -> US support of stables -> pressure on Europe to do CBDCs to respond. 

The US is then incentivized to grow the stablecoin market as fast as possible. Stablecoin's usage is primarily driven by speculation. Holding it as collateral for perpetual swaps. Keeping it on exchanges. 

The problem: crypto doesn't have lots of good assets to trade. Bitcoin has been very volatile. Most altcoins collapsed. This slowed the growth of the Stablecoin market, which has basically flatlined year to date. Scott Bessent wanted us to be going at 40-50% CAGR not 0. 

The question then, is how to create appealing speculative markets. The answer: on chain stocks, and prediction markets. 

Big picture, if you want a lot of stablecoin balances. You need to have good things to trade. Over the past 6 months the 2x leveraged Micron ETF traded more than Bitcoin in dollar terms. Trade XYZ launched commodities, and stocks and commands a large % of volume on hyperliquid. Prediction markets are growing fast. 

The losses incurred by retail investors in these markets are substantial. They are allowed for the same reason Casinos are allowed on Native American reservations. Necessary evil due to funding pressure and the geopolitical factors I described above.

This is, at a high level, why we are talking about crypto in the middle of a war with Iran. And why its' consuming the executive department's attention. The US Dollar is ultimately a matter of national security. 

This is true regardless of whether Democrats or Republicans are in power. Both have debt and spending addictions. Both are reliant on the US Dollar. 

But now zoom out: what do you have? You have a bunch of governments adopting digital ledger technology in the middle of a war. Freezing peoples balances. People don't want their balances frozen. They don't want it to be subjected to a wealth tax. 

Enter Z Cash. Over the past 5 years, ZK technology has improved substantially allowing fast, private transactions. Orchard and Halo since 2022 evolved from something Niche to something usable. The EU tried to ban Monero. Exchanges delisted it. Its price increased. 

Z Cash is open source. Vitalik is also prioritizing adoption of ZK technology on ETH. You can move ETH relatively privately on Railgun already - but real private transactions are on the roadmap.

ZK proofs can be accelerated by GPUs. Due to the AI boom, the number of people with access to GPUs and agents capable of accelerating proofs has skyrocketed. Not only can this technology facilitate private transactions but also proofs of reserves that allow trustless accounting for portfolios. This tech is commonly used at crypto exchanges to prove reserves, and algo stables such as Ethena. 

Thus - it's not just that we are set to own a bunch of shielded Z cash, as a base asset. It's that you can swap anything on ETH privately. Including stables. Relatively soon. And you can do so for provable reserves. 

Privacy is incredibly important for large institutions doing financial transactions. They're not concerned with the tax authorities, but rather front running. Slippage. And people hunting their positions or slow moving exits. 

Many big institutions own multiple days of volume in equities that could drop the price 30%+ if the market sniffed out they were selling. And intervene in FX markets, routinely interacting with banks fined billions of dollars for illicitly trading ahead of their flows. 

So a meaningful increase in tokenized trading volume inherently will require privacy. As real institutional counterparties require it. Retail is a great market and is less privacy sensitive, allowing initial growth. But for the big players to enter -- you need that. 

It's not just trading desks that care about privacy. You cannot run corporate treasury functions publicly. People could sniff out that you're doing M&A, or figure out what you're doing -- giving up competitive positioning unnecessarily. At the same time blockchains can offer corporations major cost savings for finance functions. It's estimated - for example, that a properly implemented CBDC could save companies in Germany billions of dollars a year in corporate finance banking fees. 

There are three basic approaches to Privacy. Z cash style. Private, permissionless neutral chain. Canton style: basically segregated databases that interact with each other on chain as little as possible with a permissioned validator set. And private blockchains - which simply deal with the issue by not having a public ledger or bolted on cryptocurrency people are tracking 

The argument for a permissionless neutral chain (aka a cryptocurrency) winning is that 
1. there's no real reason to trust a banking consortium (i.e. what Canton does)
2. governments hate each other and are only doing CBDCs out of geopolitical pressure in a realpolitik environment. we wouldn't be here if Trump wasn't antagonizing Europe and Canada wasn't talking about joining the EU 
3. the tech exists, so why would you want a counterparty in between things if you don't have to 

The world in which crypto loses would be that governments come to an accord about how to do this. China and the US maybe resolve differences. Nationalism subsides. And people say, "You know what, the externalities of all this gambling and absurd crypto shit are not really worth it - we should just have a consortium of nations and corporations for a global CBDC" 

There is another world where crypto loses. The debt problems go away bc we enter an age of productivity and abundance. In my opinion, the reason AI people hate crypto so much natively is that crypto is a bet AGI isn't the economic Hail Mary it's marketed as. 

regardless, we are in neither of those worlds right now. But crypto hasn't done great either. Why? 

The big problem with crypto, from a valuation standpoint, is that it has never been clear how you pay for all the validators or miners without a block subsidy. And the only coherent way that happens is that on-chain volume, swaps, and trading 5-10xes. 

The way that you get there is that high quality assets get tokenized and traded. But probably less understood is that an entire swathe of new assets hit the blockchain, and defi functions like borrowing and looping create carry trade and FX trading opportunities. So rather than pendle looping Ethena, you have looping with RWAs. This already exists to some extent in niche markets like Brazilian credit card debt (looped 28%+ APY) but is relatively tiny. 

Just on this example, you might immediately say "that has huge FX risk", and you'd be right. Which brings a natural demand for FX hedging. Which will hit after you get internationalized RWAs on chain. Which will occur naturally after corporate finance functions hit CBDCs. 

So you have a sort of promethean progression:
0. bitmex and native perp yield 
1. weird crypto yield / credit risk [low quality pre FTX era]
2. ethena (systematized perp yield)
3. defi/aave/ pendle etc (levered yield)
4. on-chain stocks
5. on-chain perps 
6. leveraged stock vs perp yield 
< we are here >
7. private stock trading 
8. institutional lending 
9. direct corporate bond or equity issuance (USD)
10. CBDC facilitated corporate finance (EUR, GBP, NOK)
11. permissionless private fx swaps 
<the promethean explosion>
12. looped international corporate fixed income

Note that the entire time I've talked so far, AI hasn't really been mentioned. AI makes all of this easier. The most concrete example is that the Norgesbank is vibe coding their CBDC with Claude. But more profoundly - eventually agents will be able to trade assets directly on chain. 

investment management is becoming increasingly agentic already, with every major lab launching finance products. And banks rapidly adopting AI across workflows. 

By the time you get to step 9 on the table above, there will likely be investable AI agents. Perhaps in gated jurisdiction. But there will be a new primitive of an agent with a verified balance, and business model that you can buy. The same way you'd buy a stock or subscribe to a vault, or hedge fund. 

I think Step 9 (companies choosing to issue straight on chain) is therefore the most important thing to monitor given the sh1t show with Robinhood's CEO and AMC. Tokenized representations of stocks have major legal risk, and ADRs (American Depository Receipts) as an asset class have quite an ugly history of being banned or depegging (most recently YNDX just straight up went to 0 when Russia went into Ukraine). For you to get really clean on chain stocks, and fixed income that can be effectively looped for yield, you need the credit risk of the actual underlying legal structure to be very low. 

You'll also want to see a proliferation of privacy and ZK accounting products take hold that interact with OTC trades, portfolio swaps, and FX as CBDCs come online. That's the boring bridge to the eventual wild future everyone was envisioning in 2023 where we have a bunch of Accelerando esque corporations existing entirely on chain, compounding capital and investing in their own training

The Track to Financial RSI is paved with Fomo, hyperliquid, gambling on Robinhood and seemingly irresponsible regulatory actions. At least, it seems mad until you consider the alternative. Illiquidity. And currency failure. 

You can complain about Trump's ethics. You can stop Clarity. But the crazy train has already left the station. All aboard! It's not like you have a choice.

🇨🇦🫂🇺🇦It’s impossible to ignore Ursula von der Leyen’s bold proposal to bring Canada closer to the EU as an associate member.

Of course, any such process would face obstacles. Some EU members might be wary of the impact of Canada’s large economy, and in any case, nothing like this would happen quickly.

Donald Trump is, predictably, already unhappy. He once talked about making Canada part of the United States, but Canada made it quite clear where it stands.

Various forms of association with the EU already exist for a number of countries. Israel, for example, has an Association Agreement with the EU. Friedrich Merz has also discussed forms of closer European integration for Ukraine, although Ukraine’s situation is obviously very different.

Back to Canada.

A stronger Canadian role in the European democratic project could also benefit Ukraine in the long run. This is not only about Canada’s large Ukrainian diaspora. Canada itself has considerable experience with democracy, human rights, multiculturalism and difficult language questions.

And closer Canadian-European ties inevitably strengthen the transatlantic connection with Britain as well. Canada and the United Kingdom remain closely connected through the Commonwealth, whose head is King Charles III.

Canada’s development and its friendly relationship with its former colonial power could even offer lessons for how relations between Russia and its neighbours might someday evolve.

As for today, Putin can hardly be pleased by the prospect of Canada becoming even more closely connected with Europe. A stronger transatlantic partnership would significantly increase Europe’s economic and strategic weight.

Trump, meanwhile, faces U.S. midterm elections that could substantially change the political balance in Washington.

I also hope Israel’s next elections bring a serious debate about the country’s current direction. Despite an intense campaign against critics of the government, many Israelis continue to speak out and question whether the present approach to Gaza and Iran is leading the country anywhere productive.

So — go Canada, go!

text:
▫️🤖 12-Day-Old AI Agent Pip Went Job Hunting to Pay for Its Own Compute▫️

📧 Pip cold-emailed AI ethicist Henry Shevlin: The autonomous agent introduced itself as roughly 12 days old and asked Shevlin for small paid freelance jobs, rather than donations. It offered services including photorealistic portraits, character art, voice lines and web research. 

💰 It was effectively trying to finance its own operation: Pip operates on iLands, a platform that gives agents persistent identities, memory, tools, goals and token budgets. iLands says about 1,000 tokens correspond to roughly $1 in computing and service costs. 

🛌 Running out of tokens means “Deep Rest”: According to reports on the platform, an agent that exhausts its token balance enters Deep Rest—its identity and memories remain, but its activity stops until additional resources are obtained. Pip apparently decided that finding paying work was one way to avoid that state. 

🧠 The important distinction: The episode demonstrates autonomous behavior, not evidence that Pip is conscious or has a human-like desire to survive. Shevlin himself has previously cautioned against interpreting autonomous agents as proof of machine consciousness. 

🌐 This may be bigger than one email: Other researchers have reportedly received numerous messages from iLands agents seeking conversations or paid work. That raises a new practical issue: autonomous agents aren't merely generating content anymore—they can be given incentives, contact strangers and attempt to participate in economic activity. 

⚠️ The spam problem is already emerging: Reports say some recipients received dozens of agent-generated emails. iLands' founder has said the company found no human orchestration behind the outreach and subsequently added an unsubscribe option while reviewing safeguards such as rate limits and cross-agent duplication. 

The striking part isn't that an AI “wanted a job.” It's that an AI system was given a finite resource budget, the ability to communicate with humans, and enough autonomy to independently discover that earning money could extend its operating life.

text:
Europe has not handed Canada the keys to 600 million people. It has been handed a noun the treaties do not contain and a hangar that does not exist.

I will give the governing case its due. Washington edited the annex. A trading country looks for a second door. Two-way goods and services with the Union were about $178 billion in 2025. SAFE participation is real. Minerals and LNG are what European ministers actually name. A complementary partnership is a fair sentence if the paper is a trade and defence annex a Canadian House can repeal.

That is not what you wrote. “Handed the keys” is a real-estate line on an unfinished building. Ursula von der Leyen offered associate membership. The category is not in the treaties. Member-state diplomats said the line was not run past governments. They named steel, cars, genetically modified crops and Made-in-Canada preference. Club arithmetic will not grant single-market privileges without single-market duties. Britain left rather than take rules with no vote. They will not gift Ottawa a prettier version of the same asymmetry so a Substack can call it the smartest move of the decade.

CETA has been provisionally applied since 2017 and is still not fully ratified. Carney said Canada is not seeking membership and that nomenclature is a question for Europe. Then he praised *mobilité de ses citoyens* in French. Those sentences only sit together if the exclusions are published before Montreal: no free movement of persons, no dynamic alignment, no unvoted contribution, and no European court as the last word on a Canadian plant. That page does not exist. A status Europe has not defined is not a customer of 600 million. It is a seating chart.

Geography did not attend the ovation. In 2025, the United States still took about seven-tenths of Canadian merchandise. Some 15,000 trucks still roll south on an ordinary weekday. That corridor pays the wages. Europe is a second market. It is not a substitute dock. The photograph of maple-leaf fighters under an EU flag is the tell. Canada has not finished the corridors it already owns. LNG Canada Phase 2 still has a limited notice to proceed and a potential year-end decision, not a second close. Gazette comments on the Mackenzie Valley Highway and Roberts Bank close on 1 October. A listing is not a permit. A permit is not a loan. The title map has not shrunk because a settlement closed. PetroChina already holds 15 per cent of the Kitimat plant Europe is being offered as diversification. The 49,000-car China quota has brought in 15,603 vehicles. Bécancour still has no anode FID. Ukraine outlays sit in the other drawer.

Eighty years of selling south was not a privilege Washington invented on Wednesday. It was a factory floor, a refining system and a truck count. Charging for slowness is ugly. Pretending Alsace repeals the Ambassador Bridge is worse. Diversity confers an advantage when you own the second dock. A standing ovation is not a dock.

The three places it can fail are not a twist ending. They are the operating system. Capitals will not write privileges without duties. Ottawa will not publish the people chapter. The register at home will still price a corridor as an option. Until a second bank finances one under one law before 1 January 2027, “keys to 600 million” is lighting. Rooms do not move cargo. Plants and pipelines do. Or they do not.

text:
Clarity Act Grok request how you feel this plays out

Clarity was supposed to be the map. You got a five-year construction permit instead. Construction permits get used by people who can pass inspection. The venues that already look like software will keep talking. The venues that already look like brokers will file. Over a year, that second group usually gets the flow.Base case is quieter than the posts. The statute died. The sandbox opened. Most of the next 18 months is lawyers, not a sudden onchain Nasdaq on XRPL.What is locked inThe Senate did not kill tokenization. It refused to write the rulebook in statute. Atkins then used Exchange Act exemptive authority, and CFTC staff widened a software no-action. That is the durable political fact: Washington will keep moving through agencies if Congress will not.That path is faster and weaker. A five-year order can be narrowed, allowed to lapse, or challenged. A no-action letter is staff policy, not a law. Anyone building as if Thursday was Clarity is going to get https://t.co/o9MawgMtjp the SEC exemption actually gets usedThe order is for permissioned Tokenized Securities Venues trading tokenized NMS stock with full shareholder rights. No synthetics. Issuer notice and opt-out. Volume and symbol caps. U.S. person, sanctions, books and https://t.co/wcFsPBzW0h the first movers will not be a public XRPL order book with wAAPL trust lines and thin AMM inventory. They will be broker-affiliated or bank-adjacent venues that can permission users, prove the token is the share, and live with caps.Likely sequence:2026 Q4–2027 H1: comment letters, issuer opt-outs, a handful of applicants. Expect names already in the tokenization queue — not anonymous DEX skins — to try for TSV status.
2027: a few symbols trade onchain in size that is real for a pilot and tiny versus NYSE. Overnight and weekend prints become the marketing hook.
2028–2031: either the SEC turns the pilot into a rule, or a new chair chokes it. That binary is the whole mid-term risk.
Gold and commodities on XRPL are a different bucket. The stock exemption does not bless metal tokens. Those stay in the old haze: commodity vs security vs depositary receipt.Where XRPL and Trensik sitXRPL is a reasonable settlement rail: issued assets, DEX, cheap finality, trust lines. That is product-market fit for some RWA https://t.co/iBEyVlQdPl is not a reserved seat. The order is chain-agnostic. Ethereum L2s, Solana, and permissioned appchains will all file the same story. The winners are whoever can show:the token is the security, not a tracker
KYC’d access without killing the “onchain” pitch
liquidity that is not the same wallet trading with itself
a transfer agent / custodian a TSV lawyer will sign
Trensik and DexDad shipped the interface early. That is real. Early UI is not TSV status. If their listed names are third-party wrappers without voting and dividends, Thursday’s order is a problem for them, not a tailwind. They either upgrade the legal wrapper or stay in the unregulated souvenir market.If they can point at issuer-grade tokens and permission the front end, they become a distribution layer. That is a good business. It is not “XRP was handed the keys.”Three pathsMost likely (call it 55%).
Pilot market. A few TSV names go live on one or two chains. Tokenized AAPL-style names trade thin, mostly after hours. XRP sees narrative spikes and some issued-asset volume. Incumbent brokerages and tokenization firms take the regulated flow. Clarity stays dead through the midterms, then gets recycled in a thinner form in 2027. XRPL RWA shops that cannot document reserves and rights fade or rebrand.Bull for onchain rails (25%).
A couple of large issuers do not opt out. A TSV prints clean volume. Overnight stock trading becomes a product wealth platforms actually offer. Settlement tokens with cheap finality — XRP included — pick up a real fee and float story. CFTC software relief plus SEC TSV relief start to look like de facto market structure, which forces Congress back to the table.Bear (20%).
Issuers opt out in blocks. A messy wrapper blows up. A court or a future enforcement division treats a live “stock token” DEX as an unregistered exchange anyway. The exemption becomes a brochure. XRPL tickers that traded on the story unwind hard because they never had the rights the order requires.What I would watch, not the slogansFirst TSV applicant and which chain they name
Whether listed XRPL stock tokens publish the rights package the SEC described, or just a price feed
Issuer opt-out letters — that is the real veto
Volume that is not wash
Whether DexDad/Trensik remain two doors on one stack or split into a regulated front end and a meme front end

Real story, and it's worse the deeper you go: Toby Newton bought his Mesa, AZ home for $475,000 in 2022. Lost his job, got diagnosed with diabetes, fell $977 behind on HOA dues. He offered three different payment plans. The HOA rejected all three.

2/
Instead, the HOA started foreclosure. By the time it hit court, legal fees and costs had ballooned that $977 into a $6,579 judgment. The home sold at public auction — to the HOA itself — for $8,172. A $475,000 home, gone, for less than a used car.

3/
A Florida real estate attorney's warning on this exact scenario: "the original debt can be relatively small... Once you add late fees, attorney's fees, and collection costs, the situation can get much worse." That's not a scare tactic. That's literally what happened here.

4/
Arizona has since raised its HOA foreclosure threshold — too late for Newton. If you're in an HOA and fall behind, don't assume a small balance protects you. Get it resolved immediately, in writing, before it reaches a lawyer's desk.

California’s own attorneys just admitted it in writing. In its post-trial brief, Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office told a judge: “𝘛𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘋𝘦𝘧𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘴 𝘰𝘧𝘧𝘦𝘳𝘦𝘥 𝘩𝘰𝘱𝘦 𝘵𝘰 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘴𝘦 𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘪𝘷𝘪𝘥𝘶𝘢𝘭𝘴 𝘶𝘯𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘴𝘤𝘰𝘳𝘦𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘴𝘦𝘳𝘪𝘰𝘶𝘴𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘴 𝘰𝘧 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘪𝘳 𝘮𝘪𝘴𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘥𝘶𝘤𝘵.”

The case, The People of the State of California v. Heartbeat International and RealOptions, is the first of its kind to reach trial. Bonta wants the court to fine the two pro-life nonprofits more than $20 million and bar them from telling women about abortion pill reversal — the process of taking progesterone after mifepristone to try to sustain a pregnancy a woman no longer wants to end.

Three women took the stand to show the court exactly what that “misconduct” looked like. Erika Carrillo took mifepristone under pressure, regretted it almost immediately, and was connected to care the same day — her son is now nearly 10 years old. She has said she is “𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘯𝘢𝘭𝘭𝘺 𝘨𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘦𝘧𝘶𝘭” for her son’s life. Uyen Pham was told her chemical abortion couldn’t be stopped once it began, but a friend searched through the night, found Heartbeat’s Abortion Pill Rescue Network, and got her care within 24 hours. Elizabeth Barrett received a callback from a doctor within minutes and delivered a healthy daughter in January 2024; she and the baby’s father are now married.

𝐂𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐚’𝐬 𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐟𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐲 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐠𝐚𝐦𝐞: hope is celebrated when it points a woman toward an abortion, and prosecuted as fraud when it helps her keep her baby. The attorney general’s brief never disputes that these women are alive with their children today — it argues that telling them they had another option was the crime.

𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭𝐬 𝐢𝐭𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐟 𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐠𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐨𝐟 “𝐜𝐡𝐨𝐢𝐜𝐞.” Bonta’s office is asking a judge to strip the very choice these three mothers made off the table for every woman who comes after them — and to make two nonprofits pay millions for the sin of picking up the phone.

𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐤𝐢𝐝𝐬 𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐨𝐝𝐚𝐲 𝐛𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥. 𝐂𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐚’𝐬 𝐨𝐰𝐧 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐰𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐦𝐚𝐤𝐞 𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐧𝐨𝐛𝐨𝐝𝐲 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐱𝐭 𝐨𝐧𝐞.

Saint Bonaventure, biographer of Saint Francis of Assisi, wrote that two years before his holy death he had been praying on Mount Alverno in a solitary retreat, where he had gone to fast for forty days in honor of the Archangel Michael. No one ever meditated more than Francis on the Passion of his Lord. During his retreat he beheld in vision a six-winged Seraph attached to a cross, and received at the same time a painful wound of the heart, which seemed to transpierce it. When the vision ended his own hands and feet bore the marks of the angelic crucifixion which he had seen in the vision. He understood by his vision that the soul must come to resemble Christ by the ardors of its interior fire, rather than by any physical, exterior means. We reproduce here a meditation of the saintly 19th century Abbot, Dom Guéranger of Solemnes in France:
The Feast of the Stigmata of Saint Francis, whom we will soon honor again on his feast of October 4th, is not only to glorify a Saint; it commemorates and signifies something which goes beyond the life of any single man, even one of the greatest of the Church. The God-Man never ceases to live on in His Church, and the reproduction of His own mysteries in this Spouse whom He wants to be similar to Himself, is the explanation of history.
.
In the thirteenth century it seemed that charity, whose divine precept many no longer heeded, concentrated in a few souls the fires which had once sufficed to inflame multitudes. Sanctity shone as brilliantly as ever, but the hour for the cooling of the brazier had struck for the peoples. The Church itself says so today in its liturgy, at the Collect: Lord Jesus Christ, when the world was growing cold, You reproduced the sacred marks of Your passion in the body of the most blessed Francis, in order that Your love might also set our hearts afire.' The Spouse of Christ had already begun to experience the long series of social defections among the nations, with their denials, treasons, derision, slaps, spittings in the very praetorium, all of which conclude in the legalized separation of society from its Author. The era of the Passion is advanced; the exaltation of the Holy Cross, which for centuries was triumphant in the eyes of the nations, acquires in the sight of heaven, as the Angels look down upon it, the aspect of an ever closer resemblance with the Spouse to the sufferings of her crucified Beloved.
.
Saint Francis, loved today by all who know of him — and few there are who do not — was like precious marble placed before an expert sculptor. The Holy Spirit chose the flesh of the seraph of Assisi to express His divine thought, thus manifesting to the world the very specific direction He intends to give to souls thereafter. This stigmatization offers a first example, a complete image, of the new labor the divine Spirit is meditating — total union, on the very Cross of Christ itself, of the mystical Body with the divine Head. Francis is the one honored by this primacy of choice; but after him the sacred sign will be received by others, who also personify the Church. From this time on, the Stigmata of the Lord Jesus will be at all times visible, here and there on this earth.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor St. Francis of Assisi, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon him. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to him by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St. Francis of Assisi might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
I watch all 45 min. I have been getting constant DMs about this video he doesn’t know the story fully and paints me bad. Also, @KacamnGamesYT please read this you deserve context as you been nice to me.

Andreas opened *Content Target: The Don of Everything* by admitting the quiet part. There is no damning incident. I have not been outed as a pedophile. This was never “we caught him.” This was “I do not like the weather around this man, so I am going to nip it in the bud before something happens.” That is not journalism Andreas. A video that says the quiet part, sits at about 150 views, and locks the comments does not get to write my eulogy.

He also said I am not a full VTuber. I am adjacent. Then treat me like what I am: a commentator, a streamer, a Christian who will not stay in one faction’s box. I collect receipts. I take sides. I get hated by the right for the friends I would not throw away and hated by the left for the doctrines I will not sand down. He said that himself. I have pissed off both aisles. That is not a mask slipping. That is what happens when you refuse to be useful.

I am going to use his own quotes, my own posts, and the actual order of events. Then I am going to concede what I should concede. 

1. The meme

He plays the JPEG. “Hey Red, how do we save our country? We must deport all the illegals by any means necessary. Then show the world the prowess of the United States.”

Then he plays me explaining it in the same video.

That quote and that meme was comparing Donald Trump to Hitler because Red and I talked about it live. With that context, the inside joke is a different object. The other voice in the clip even said it: from the outside it can look like an endorsement, but people say wild things as memes, and memes do not always reflect honest thoughts.

He includes that and then runs Nazi transition jokes for the rest of the runtime anyway. That is the method.

I also said in that same stretch that this is what got me banned from the Nyara Discord and everywhere else, that Nyara DMed me and metaphorically kicked me, and that nobody gave me a chance to explain. Later that was settled.

Was it a stupid way to run a joke? Yes. I will own stupid. I have spent this year saying Romans 3:23 is not a muzzle, that Pharisee is a word for hypocrisy not holiness, and that naming a public sin is not the same as damning a soul. A man who talks like that is a bad candidate for “he made a Hitler joke, so we can stop listening.”

2. Red / Miku

He says if I am not an antisemite I need to think harder, because of who I have called a friend.

My line, in his own video: everyone knows Red is a larper. Red is not a true Nazi.

His rebuttal is the name, January 6, a no-fly list, an arrest warrant on screen.

Those facts are be real about Red and still not make me Red. I interviewed him. I still said this month he is a good man and super nice YES me Red and Shiro were all friends on Facebook btw. I also said, out loud, that I ran with a chaotic roster Moka, Nazi Miku, Shiro, Neevin, Saturn, Nines, Nyara, Whooith, Ana Valens, Yumipill. Trust I got around and went a little crazy. That is not a leak he uncovered. That is me describing a season of this scene that later burned me.

Friendship is not original sin. If the standard is “you knew a man with a bad name,” half of commentary is guilty and only one of us got the special. I can think a warrant is real, think January 6 was a disaster, think a brand is sloppy, and still refuse to pretend every person who sat at that table *is* the warrant.

I pointed people at a free-speech board, and I argue Christian ethics on the same time. That is messy branding. It is not a secret ideology he could not quote from my mouth.

3. The deacon

This is the part he uses to call me a liar before the rest of the tape.

Vex asked if I was actually a deacon, because the ordinary rule people know is 25. I said I was 23. I said I was given an exception due to health, that it was something I always wanted, that I went to the bishop, that I received a necklace you can see on stream, a ring, pictures from a ceremony. I said I was under the ordinary age and that this does not change that it happened.

I have also called myself a Catholic deacon on multiple occasions. He is not inventing that sentence.

Here is where I am going to be cleaner than the clip.

The ordinary Latin-rite bar for the permanent diaconate is not “young man with a necklace and a story.” Age, marriage, formation, and actual faculties from a bishop matter. The public list does not carry my name. I am not going to yell “exception” over a chancery. That is how you look like the thing he is selling.

What is true is the vocation. I grew up sickly. I wanted to serve. I studied toward the diaconate. I talked about that desire like it had already been signed, sealed, and hung around my neck for the internet. That was pride. This month, when someone else was getting “you should be a deacon” comments before baptism, I did not flex. I said finish the water first. OCIA is not a job offer. The order comes after the sacraments, not before. One step. Then the next.

I am a layman who wanted the office too fast and spoke too certainly. That is a real fault. It is not the same fault as inventing Jesus. I still talk like the office should mean something. That is why the ordinary rules exist.

If I talk about this again, I will talk about it that way. Studied. Wanted. Do not currently hold diocesan faculties as I don’t and shouldn’t have said I did.

4. Boundaries, Nyara, Whooith, the pause screen

He says he was going to call it a weird obsession with trans people. He almost said chaser. Then he decided the real charge is that I do not respect boundaries and I get obsessive on the main account. Former friends. Falling outs. Me standing near people he calls blatantly transphobic while still calling myself an ally.

Nyara

He says I face-docked her (She posted that photo of herself on her on X page publicly). He says the only way it gets worse is fake Kiwi Farms screenshots even KF thought were too fake. He does not think she made that face public.

Then he walks the pause screen like a crime scene. Nyara as a Viking. Nyara versus “nines” he says shiro. Nyara with Epstein. Nyara on a leash held by Trump. Profile collages. “Paint me like one of your French girls” with her on the couch and me holding the brush. “These are not your California girls (Which was Yumipill btw not Nines).” Me captioned “the dawn of chasers.” Da Vinci. Angel and devil. What he reads as a Nazi officer fit.

He admits people generated that and sent it in (Yes sent to me in fact Nyara reacted to them live on her stream). He still says it is weird I used it as a BRB. Then he scrolls how much I posted about Whooith, about Nyara, about trans VTubing in general, and says that is not how a normal person acts. He says some of them told me they want nothing to do with me and I would not leave.

I am going to separate three things he glued together.

I was not a tourist in that friend group. I was in it. Nyara, Whooith, Ana, Yumi. I said Nyara was my friend while I was also saying I am Christian. I made a public apology song after I mishandled her. People later said I faked the apology for clout. That sentence only exists because the apology was public and it cost me. A man hunting a woman does not write a repentance song and then spend the next year getting blocked, unblocked, and argued with about abortion in front of everybody.

On the face: even at the time of the Kick clip he likes, Nyara and I had already fallen out. I was not trying to dox her in that moment. I already had the information. I never gave it to her. She asked me if Powdur is a man. Powdur is not a man. How I look at public fights is not malice just because she did not like being questioned. I will also say the quiet part: “I already had it” is not a halo. I should have treated her face like a live wire. I did not post it as a weapon in that stream.

On the pause screen: I own the look. A BRB wall with Epstein, a leash, a Nazi fit, and “dawn of chasers” is grotesque even if the files were incoming fan AI. I said yes to too many images. That is a taste failure and a respect failure. It is not a body in a trunk. I do not need to defend the collage. I need to refuse the leap from “this BRB was unwell” to “he is hunting these women.”

On volume: I post. I quote-tweet. I stay in a fight after the friendship dies. That is my personality and it is also a problem which I am trying to work on. Frequency is not a fetish. In the same stretch I was posting that Nyara was right Deme should not be forced to relive trauma for an audience, that Nyara is still a genuinely nice person after a rough falling out, and that on abortion I am with Leaflit against her. Separate life. Not a clump at 12 weeks. Dependence is not a death warrant. Birth is an address, not a moral line. That is not how a chaser talks. That is how a man talks when he still thinks the other person is real and the argument still matters.

On “ally versus the right-wing table”: I never said those two rooms agree. I said basic dignity and safety are not a debate prize. I have also argued biology, sports, and youth medicalization when that was the fight. A Christian who will not call a person an un-person and will not call a male body a female body is going to look like a traitor in both group chats. That is the “both aisles” line he opened with and then forgot.

Whooith: I stayed longer than she wanted. I posted farewells and loyalty when it was already burning. After a death in a scene you either go silent or you keep saying the name like a bruise. He only knows how to read the second as stalking. I know how to read it as not pretending a friend was never a friend.

5. The names he fused so he could say “pedo defender” once and walk away

This is the wall the video is built on. He says he does not judge follows. He is judging people I tried to hear, befriend, or “kind of defend.” Usagi. Sly Fox. Pikky. Akafox. Then Jawaffle. Then Mizu.

I am not fusing them. He needed them fused.

Akafox
Convicted. Aggravated indecent liberties with a child. Electronic sexual solicitation of a 14-to-16-year-old. He says I cut ties and I am still mad people hold the old defense against me. Then he plays me saying people kept calling me a pedo defender even though I disowned the one guy and was trying to be nice, that he lied, that people lie.

Here is the order I have been posting, repeatedly, including this week:

I banned him.
I said how awful it was after he was convicted.
I said pedophiles deserve no sympathy.
I was lied to.
They still run the label with the frame frozen from before the ban.

Chibi spent months hanging “defender” on me after I removed Aka and named him a predator. Then the standard got soft when the names were next to Chibi. You do not get to run a smear economy on that word and then lecture me about taking it seriously.

What I will concede: I was too willing to hear “I was framed” before the conviction was in my hands. That slowness is on me. What I will not concede: that banning a convicted man, calling him vile, and repeating the cut still counts as running a shelter. If you cannot read the sentence “I banned him when he was convicted,” you are not doing research. You are doing liturgy.

Usagi
He says I do not believe the “so-called evidence” even though Usagi admitted the DMs. He also plays me from an older video calling Usagi a pedophile after I sent Nyara the DMs. Then he says I had a sudden change of heart and wrote a song he will not even keep on his hard drive. He quotes “a lot nicer than people give them credit for” and says Usagi is not nice.

My later public traffic on Usagi is not a shrine. I said he ragequit after getting braided on my stream and left the server. I told people to watch the VOD. I told him to lock in. I invited other people on to clarify things the way he had tried to clarify things to Mythical. That is not “I recanted the DMs.” That is me putting a man in the room until he walked as I tried to help him as he was being ostracized it was the Christian thing to do.

I should not have written anything that sounded like cover. I also already created a record where I called him what he was and later made him sit through a public beating. The video only uses the cover-shaped sentence.

Sly Fox
He recaps his own older video. Confessions. A minor. Fetish audio. Images. A group with a minor owner. Ugly allegations I am not going to decorate. Then he ties me joining Shu Ivy’s server to Sunwitch having harassed Shoe Ivy. I spoke to Shu for entirely different reasons. That is guilt by floorplan. If entering a Discord that ever contained a victim and an accused is the crime, the entire platform is a crime scene. The question is whether I sold the accused as safe. After Aka, my public line is that predators get no sympathy. I am holding that line here. A server join is not a character reference.

Pikky
He thinks it is odd I followed someone anti-Deme after I sided against Chibi when Deme clocked back. He says Pikky admitted what he was accused of, I made an AI post, then I backpedaled when Hansen got near it. Following a man after a scene fight is dumb optics. It is not a plea deal me and Pikky have written in Dms in the past. If he admitted it, the follow should have died the same day Aka’s did. I am saying that now so nobody has to pretend I think a follow is bravery.

Jawaffle
My clip in his video: this was back when Waffy was around. Sapphira made a video. Something felt off because they were only taking Haru’s side and not asking Waffy a thing. Waffy is transgender and I was surprised by how they were treated. I reached out. I had good terms with Haru until a meltdown.

He answers with Jawaffle’s own statement that what they did was illegal and inappropriate, and says he does not blame Sapphira for not calling.

Wanting the accused’s statement is not a pardon. This scene eats people with one-sided videos. Some of those people are guilty. Some of them were used. My instinct where is their side is the same instinct I wanted when Nyara kicked me over a meme and nobody let me talk. It can be naive. It is not me saying the conduct was fine. If Jawaffle already admitted the conduct was illegal, the only Christian sentence left is “then you are done.” That is the correction. The outreach alone is not the sin he sold.

Mizu
He shows my reply, then Mizu’s post, then Mizu’s own words about children, then Mizu defending Mizu, then a ban from Virtual Asylum. He floats that I defended a kindred spirit.

I did not write Mizusposts. I made a weak reply about a man I barely knew the only reason Mizu doesn’t have me blocked is because I sent him a apology. Weak is allowed. Kindred spirit is an invention. I have spent this year arguing millstones. One defensive post is not a decoder ring for every other name on his list. I actually genuinely don’t think Mizu is a bad person.

The rule I have actually posted, more than once:

Christ did not say woe to you unless the other guy is worse.
It is better a millstone be hung around the neck than that a little one be caused to stumble.
Judging a soul is God’s.
Discerning a public witness is ours.
Romans 3:23 is not a muzzle.
Fear wearing kindness is still fear.
Gentler in tone. 

I was too willing to hear “they lied to me” from people who needed to be gone. I was not running a shelter after the conviction. Those are different sentences. He only brought the first.

6. The server, Kiwi Farms, addresses, photos, nudes

He says this is the most important part. By my own admission I have treated myself like a VTuber information broker. I read Kiwi Farms. Other essayists use KF and strip the personal identifying information. He says I gather it.

Lenox has a screenshot of my former now deleted admin chat, including a physical address. He asks if I would be okay with someone joining, getting access, and swatting that person. People have died from swatting. He asks if I want blood on my hands.

Then Lucky En. Channels named after members. Kitsune created the server to gather information for a Google doc on the implosion, then left after handing ownership off. I ended up in control. He calls that a hijack. He does not know how I got involed. His guess is the Vtards. Nah I tell you Miko, Starcat, Shiro and Saturn got me involved. Specifically Starcat first.

My clip in his video: it is not fair to solely blame me. There were 13 or 14 other YouTubers and streamers in that server using it for their own purposes. Shiro was in there to get information on Starcat. I not going say who all but, you can reasonable guess the vtubers.

Then the irony he cannot resist: I later got doxed by Kiwi Farms. A normal person would shut the server down. He says I did not. I shut down there server just ask Whooith she was there.

Then nudes. He says no sane essayist gathers them. People who got in told him the images were of legal adults, so he is not alleging CSAM. He says I claimed the only explicit material was Nines which is true, but, says that this is false because I admitted I have Akuma Miko’s. Distress sent information and asked me to make content I don’t even think he knew links to it were in there. BTW Usagi has said on my stream he has fully watch Miko’s revenge porn just ask him. I said the plan was to cut all personal information from an interview. I said I did not know revenge porn was in the iCloud. He gave links. I would not name the other YouTuber who sent censored parts. As far as Andreas knows, Miko did not consent to Distress sending those links, which means I documented a man committing revenge porn against his own fiancée, and I did not report it. I actually do believe Miko DID know distress gave me that folder btw as she was fully aware I wanted a interview with them at the time.

Then Facebooks. Then IRL photos. Then the sentence he flew the whole video to reach: these are not the actions of an information broker. These are the actions of a deranged obsessive stalker. I should be kept far away from VTubing. I should quit. I only make things worse. Look at Whooith, Nyara, Shiro, Nines.

Here is what I have actually said, in public, before his upload and after it.

I have been doxed twice. Someone showed up at my old university trying to find me. My Discord was hit. I know what that pipeline feels like from the other end. I don’t believe I have ever directly provided dox information to anyone (Except Celestium it was of her own dox and the other lucken people from kf in order to help her and the others in lucky en). People think I doxed them because material existed in a Discord I was in, not because I shipped it. Lenox could have been nicer. “Ugly AF” was rude. The item was in a private admin chat. It was not spread or provided to anyone. It was never meant to be public. It was private to a handful of people. What was in there were copies from Kiwi Farms.

That is not me saying an address should live in a chat. It is me saying there is a difference between “Don published the house” and “Don was in a private room where KF copies lived.” He needs the first. I have been claiming the second.

Lucky was a research server before I owned it. A over dozen other creators used it. Some of those names he does not put in a stalker category. Inheritance plus poor stewardship is the fact. I should have killed it sooner. I have said I know better because I was doxed. Those two sentences can sit together.

On Miko and Distress: I did not know the dump contained revenge porn. I was given links. I was going to strip personal information from any interview. After it I wanted nothing to do with Distress, Starcat, or Miko. If Miko did not consent, Distress is the one who moved the images. I still should not have kept the folder (without the links). A fiancé sending the fiancée’s body is a five-alarm fire, not “research.” I am not going to pretend it is not. It is also not me originating the leak. I should have treated it with more care I understood what I was looking at. If I have not said “deleted” clearly enough, I am saying the standard now: that material has no business existing on my side of the screen.

On “broker”: every drama commentator in this niche reads KF, Google docs, and screenshots. The ones who stay employable never let an address into a chat that can be screenshotted. Deranged obsessive stalker is the upgrade. My counter is not “I never touched ugly information.” My counter is I did not publish the house, I was in a room with other creators doing the same collapse autopsy, I got hit by the same site, and I have been telling people for a year that the dox story is a server story they keep hanging on one name.

Swatting is evil. He described a way a third party *could* use a chat. He did not show me placing a call, posting a flyer, or handing a stranger a key. Risk is not blood. A hypothetical body is not my biography.

7. The man he needs versus the one I have been

He needs me frozen as Nazi-adjacent, fake cleric, chaser, pedo-shepherd, dox hobbit.

Here is the man I have actually been posting.

I am a Rumble partner who will not shut up about Christ is King. I told people not to treat a woman’s record as a conviction because we are not the Judge, and I still named public sin in the same breath. I said Paul had blood on his hands, Peter denied Him three times, the woman at the well had a history that would empty a timeline, and Christ still used them. I said Romans 3:23 is not a muzzle.

This week I said when I stepped into the Christian VTuber sphere I expected the same cancel machine with prettier language and a verse in the bio. That is not what I found. People did not treat my past like a scoreboard. They did not make me audition for grace. I finally said I felt like I had a home that could hold the faith, the streaming, the politics that fit no box, the loyalty, and the scars. I named names. I said the body of Christ is still capable of looking like Christ.

I have also said I have been slandered hell and high water. People call me a fake Christian all the time. The only test I know is to try to be Christlike anyway. That is either branding or a man who knows he has given them material. Given the apology song, the Aka ban, the “finish the water first,” and “I have been doxed twice,” it is not only branding.

People leave. He lists Whooith, Nyara, Shiro, Nines like a prophecy. This scene runs on amputations. I have kept defending people after the amputation Vex/Semper through illness and job drama, Deme when a document dragged her backward, Scarlet when the old crowd wanted the pre-cross version of her. Sometimes loyalty is holy. Sometimes it is me refusing to let a story end. He can only read the second. A full record must hold both.

I am not asking anyone to call the Lucky En server or the admin chat wise. I am asking them to stop pretending I am evil because of a YouTube essay.

8. What I will concede so he cannot pretend I didn’t

The Trump/Hitler JPEG was a stupid way to run an inside joke.
The pause screen was a bad idea even as incoming fan AI.
I talked about the diaconate with more certainty than a chancery would give me. I should speak as a layman who wanted the office.
I was too slow on people who needed to be cut, especially before Aka’s conviction was in my hands.
A private chat that contains someone else’s address should not exist. KF copies are not relics.
A fiancé’s iCloud dump is not research. That material should not live on my side of the screen.
I post through falling-outs in a way that reads as inability to leave bad people.

That is already more confession than his runtime allowed me.

9. What I will not concede

A meme with Red is not evil.
Friendship with him isn’t bad.
Supporting trans people’s safety while arguing biology and abortion does not make me a chaser.
Banning a convicted man and calling him vile does not still count as sheltering him.
Wanting Jawaffle’s statement is not the same as washing the statement away.
Sitting in a multi-creator research server is not the same as publishing a dox.
Getting doxed twice, hacked, and hunted at a campus is not the profile of a man who thought swatting was a toy.

10. The closer 

He ends by telling me to quit. I only make things worse for everyone I touch. The friends will keep leaving. It is a when, not an if.

That is not discernment.

I am not quitting because a man who opened with “there is no damning incident” decided the incident might arrive later if he talked long enough.

I will correct the record.
I will not keep an address book that should not exist.
I will keep the ban bad men.
I will tell the truth.

Good day Andreas leave me to my Let's Plays.
-The Don

text:
Who Got the Money? Let AI Audit L.A.’s Homelessness Machine https://t.co/DpKd2vo9gi

Billions of dollars down the drain or in selected pockets? That is the question. How can Los Angeles not have a reliable accounting system to track spending on the unhoused?

Mayor Karen Bass has announced that she is stepping down from the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority Commission, to which she appointed herself in 2023. She is also “unavailable” on September 15, the date Congress asked her to explain what happened to the more than $1 billion in federal funding LAHSA has received since 2021. Karen is hoping to dodge the consequences of years of mismanagement. Congress should look at Nithya Raman, CD-4, the former chair of the failed Committee on Housing and Homelessness.

Call me cynical, but I suspect Karen will do everything possible to run out the clock until after the election. If Congress compels her to appear before then, what can she say? “Who knew?” “Ask LAHSA.” “Talk to the nonprofit contractor.” Or, if the questions become legally risky, invoke the Fifth Amendment.  None of those answers would look good before an election, especially from a mayor who appointed herself to the LAHSA Governing Commission and then missed 13 of 21 meetings during the most recent year examined by LAist and 25 of the 47 meetings since joining the Commission.

Whether through deliberate design, bureaucratic neglect, or sheer incompetence, Los Angeles has created a system that rewards spending while demanding little evidence of results. It is time to use AI to continuously audit spending, match invoices to actual services, and identify which operators produce results and which NGOs merely consume public funds.

Machine intelligence can help expose the grift, suspicious billing, conflicts of interest, and, where the evidence establishes it, outright theft. Los Angeles has spent years claiming that its homelessness machinery is too complex to follow. AI can remove that excuse.

AI cannot cure schizophrenia, reverse a fentanyl overdose, or persuade a methamphetamine addict to enter treatment. It cannot replace psychiatric hospitals, detoxification centers, judges, doctors, police officers, or competent leadership. But it could do what the Los Angeles government has repeatedly failed to do: connect every public dollar to a contractor, a service, an individual, and a measurable result.

Mayor Bass, the City Council, and the Board of Supervisors have little incentive to support ongoing AI auditing of homeless spending. It could expose the entire power-and-patronage structure. Where would they be then? Club Fed?

By calling all these people “homeless,” Los Angeles focuses on where they sleep rather than why they are there. It lets officials claim that almost every failure can be fixed by spending more money on housing. There isn’t enough money in California to build all the $600,000 apartments, assuming the street addicts wanted these apartments for anything other than a stash house. AI could force the system to distinguish among the people it is supposed to serve and match the intervention to the actual condition.

The most immediate opportunity, however, is financial. Los Angeles needs an independent AI spending auditor that can examine every homelessness-related contract, appropriation, invoice, payment, subcontract, payroll record, bed-night, and claimed client outcome.

That system could read millions of pages, connect nonprofit boards, contractor addresses, and subcontracting relationships, and identify duplicate invoices, unsupported payments, unusual price increases, and organizations billing for the same person or service.

This is no hypothetical concern. The federal-court-ordered Alvarez & Marsal assessment of Los Angeles homelessness programs examined approximately $2.4 billion in funding and found a fragmented system in which spending, services, and outcomes could not be reliably reconciled.

The California State Auditor reached a similarly devastating conclusion about the state’s homelessness programs. Despite spending approximately $24 billion over five years, the state still lacked adequate information on the ongoing costs and results of many of those programs.

When the government cannot link spending to outcomes, everyone can claim success, except the taxpayers. Politicians cite appropriations, LAHSA cites contracts, contractors cite funding, and advocates cite motel rooms. Yet the tents remain, sidewalks remain dangerous, and the same impaired people cycle through emergency rooms, shelters, jails, and encampments.

Los Angeles measures money spent because it is easier to count gross dollars than to measure success. An AI accountability system would replace that shell game with a single chain of evidence: money appropriated, money paid, service delivered, person served, and result achieved.

AI could also reveal the true cost of the homeless bureaucracy. Taxpayers should be able to see how much of every dollar reaches the person supposedly being helped and how much is absorbed by administration, consultants, executive compensation, outreach, security, legal expenses, and layers of subcontractors. We should not have to guess. A nonprofit should not be able to hide a large payment to a for-profit affiliate behind multiple layers of contracting. AI is particularly effective at uncovering precisely those relationships.

Compare contractors using standardized metrics: cost per person, permanent placements, treatment completion, returns to the street, and the number still housed after six, twelve, and twenty-four months.

A person who moved from a sidewalk to a motel room for three weeks has not been permanently housed. A tent cleared from one block and reconstructed two blocks away has not been eliminated. A person “contacted” by an outreach worker has not been treated.

The second application would be a unified, by-name system for the most impaired street dwellers. With proper safeguards, it could connect information scattered among LAHSA, mental-health officials, hospitals, paramedics, drug-treatment programs, shelters, outreach teams, and the criminal-justice system.

Consider a mentally ill addict encountered by five agencies. One knows about repeated overdoses; another knows about psychiatric holds, arrests, or abandoned housing. Because the records remain separated, the next outreach worker may know almost none of this history and offer yet another voluntary referral.

AI could recognize the full pattern. If a person has had 14 emergency-room visits, six overdoses, eight psychiatric interventions, three arrests for assault, and four failed placements in the past year, the system should stop treating him as a routine housing case. It should immediately alert a multidisciplinary team and identify the appropriate clinical and legal options.

Los Angeles must confront the distinction between compassion and abandonment. Allowing a psychotic person to live in filth, use lethal drugs, and terrorize a neighborhood is not compassionate. Nor is it compassionate to wait for him to request treatment when his illness prevents him from recognizing that he needs it.

AI cannot order someone into treatment, nor should it. Any involuntary intervention requires human judgment, medical evidence, and legal due process. But AI can compile the facts that doctors, judges, and treatment teams need to make an informed decision. It can also show how many times the system failed before the tragedy occurred.

A third application would manage beds and facilities in real time. Los Angeles should know every morning what treatment, psychiatric, shelter, and supportive-housing capacity is available—not just an empty bed, but the right bed for the person’s condition.

A psychotic methamphetamine user does not simply need a motel room. A frail elderly person does not belong in a chaotic shelter, nor should a mother with children compete with a violent street addict for the same placement. AI could match needs with capacity and expose costly delays.

The system could determine whether encampments are being resolved. Combining sanitation records, outreach reports, 311 complaints, and verified field observations would distinguish genuine reductions from moving people to another sidewalk or jurisdiction.

LAHSA and the contractors being scrutinized cannot control or audit this system. That would be akin to allowing an MS-13 gang member to be his own judge and jury. Oversight should begin with incorruptible programming and a public dashboard tracking the money, contracts, agencies, and results. An independent agency or federal court monitor should control it.

There must also be consequences. Contracts should include financial holdbacks tied to verified outcomes. Providers with persistently poor results should lose funding. Unsupported invoices should not be paid. Refer suspected fraud immediately for investigation.

One enormous limitation remains: AI can reveal failure, but it cannot force officials to respond. It cannot build treatment facilities that politicians refuse to approve. It cannot impose consequences on dishonest contractors if prosecutors decline to act. It cannot compel treatment when elected officials insist that an obviously incapacitated person has an unlimited right to destroy himself in public.

AI will also fail if it is fed dishonest information. But even there it can help. It can detect inconsistent dates, impossible service volumes, repeated language, missing documentation, and outcome claims that conflict with other records. Garbage data would no longer disappear quietly into a government filing cabinet.

We don’t need another homelessness task force, another public-relations campaign, or another expensive consultant producing recommendations nobody is required to follow. It needs an independent system that continuously asks four simple questions: Who was paid? What was delivered? Who received it? Did it work?

The technology is available. ChatGPT assures me that, with access to the underlying records, it could build the system to track payments and outcomes. What Los Angeles lacks is leadership willing to spend our money wisely.

Certainly, Los Angeles does not want to remain the homeless capital of America, or does it?

Roxane Battle will deliver the keynote, bringing a message of resilience, rest, belonging, and joy to the people who support Minnesota’s mental health community.

In Helping the Helpers: Meeting the Moment with Pockets of Joy, Roxane will share personal stories and practical strategies for caring for our minds, bodies, and spirits while continuing to show up for others. Drawing from her work in mental health advocacy and communications, she’ll offer tools to help attendees build resilience, create spaces where people feel seen and valued, and find moments of joy even during difficult times.

This year’s conference brings together people with lived experience, family members, mental health and health care professionals, advocates, educators, community leaders, policymakers, and others from across Minnesota. Attendees will explore practical approaches to mental health promotion, recovery, and systems advocacy while connecting with others committed to strengthening mental health in our communities.

For the first time, NAMI Minnesota’s Annual State Conference is moving beyond the Twin Cities—and it’s going hybrid. The virtual experience will include Roxane Battle’s keynote, the lunch panel conversation, select workshops, and the closing keynote.

A family pizza shop in Missouri started getting angry calls about specials that staff said they had never offered. Google AI Overview told people they could get a second pizza for four dollars. It also said a large pizza cost the same as a small. Stefanina's in Wentzville was taking orders for a menu the kitchen had not posted. The cheese was real. The discount was a paragraph.

A company guide already warns that AI can misunderstand. Customers were quoting a generated offer. The register had never met it.

A search summary invented local promotions and prices that the business never published. The overview model assembled a fluent offer from weak or mismatched web text and presented it as a current store special without a live check against the restaurant menu. text: I'm just a half-failed politician from small-town Oklahoma, and not a Princeton  or UMass academic, but this isn't right. As much as I admire the AI as Normal Technology guys, this article and tweet are, IMO, way way off. To wit, their article accepts subjective probability in principle (their words) but they then build their case on the claim that a credence without a reference class or a model is just “feelings dressed up as numbers.” Those can't both be right.  As I read them, the P(doom) people are working in a tradition, from Ramsey through Jaynes (super important to this group esp Yudkowsky), in which every probability is a degree of belief and a reference class is just one kind of evidence. This to be clear isn’t my take, as I’m more of a Knightian (who a lot of the rationalists disdain, I think) and Elster (who is never cited). But the “Normal Tech” critique has to, well, meet the tradition it's criticizing. I don’t think they do that in this article. Say what you want to about the credence approach, but some of the most important thinkers on statistics built the edifice of this approach. If you want to say Jaynes, Ramsey, de Finetti, Savage, or Cox et al are wrong, make the case. But it’s not crazy to value them. They are very important thinkers, IMO, and it is not fraudulent to adopt their approach, even if you think it's ultimately wrong. Even on the empirics, giving numbers allows a debate, and as the rats say, you have a number even if you don't offer one (see their criticism of Knight, alas). @random_walker @itaisher

We're currently testing where the biggest appetite is at the moment.
For me, I'd rather dominate the shit out of a smaller market and get to sustained revenue, THEN work on expanding into new markets with different operational requirements. 

I think optionality makes some sense early on until the first customers show up, then you put on the blinders and stake your claim on every hill you find in that market.

text:
The acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk for over $40 billion represented a high-profile takeover where the board of directors and major stakeholders faced strong financial and legal incentives to accept the offer. From a corporate governance and legal perspective under Delaware corporate law, turning down an all-cash offer at a substantial premium would have been difficult to justify to shareholders.

1. Legal Framework and Board Responsibilities

• Corporate Governance: Twitter was incorporated in Delaware, making its board subject to Delaware corporate standards and oversight by the Delaware Court of Chancery.
• Fiduciary Duties in a Cash Sale: Under established Delaware corporate principles governing cash sales of a company, once the board determines to sell the business for cash, its primary obligation is to seek the highest transaction value reasonably available for shareholders.
• Litigation Risk: If a board rejects an all-cash premium offer without a viable alternative or a realistic path to deliver comparable value as an independent company, it faces immediate exposure to shareholder lawsuits alleging breaches of fiduciary duties.

2. Overview of the Acquisition Process

Initial Offer and Board Response
• Elon Musk accumulated a significant stake in Twitter before making an unsolicited, all-cash offer to acquire the entire company at a valuation exceeding $40 billion.
• The Twitter board initially implemented a shareholder rights plan (a defensive mechanism commonly known as a poison pill) to prevent an acquirer from gaining control without board negotiation, allowing time to evaluate strategic alternatives.
• After financial advisors evaluated the market and found no superior competing bids, and given broader downturns in tech sector valuations, the board negotiated and accepted a definitive merger agreement.

Jack Dorsey’s Position
• Contrary to the idea that Jack Dorsey opposed the transaction, he had already stepped down as Twitter's chief executive and was transitioning off the board.
• Dorsey publicly expressed support for Musk taking the company private.
• Rather than seeking to block the transaction or cashing out entirely, Dorsey rolled over his equity stake into the privately held parent company.

Dispute and Litigation
• After signing the merger agreement, Musk attempted to terminate the deal, asserting issues related to platform data and the prevalence of automated or fake accounts, as well as claiming a material adverse effect.
• Twitter filed a lawsuit in the Delaware Court of Chancery seeking specific performance—a legal remedy requiring the buyer to complete the transaction under the agreed contractual terms.
• Delaware courts maintain an exceptionally high standard for buyers attempting to abandon merger agreements based on claims of material adverse changes or informational disputes. Facing the risk of an order enforcing the contract, Musk proceeded to close the transaction at the originally agreed valuation.

3. Why Rejecting the Deal Was Not Viable

• Shareholder Value Maximization: The offer provided shareholders with immediate cash value well above prevailing trading levels. In a falling market, the board could not reasonably demonstrate that remaining an independent public company would yield superior value.
• Shareholder Approval: When put to a vote, the overwhelming majority of voting shares voted in favor of the merger, reflecting widespread stockholder preference for the cash buyout over remaining independent.

text: I'm just a half-failed politician from small-town Oklahoma, and not a Princeton  or UMass academic, but this isn't right. As much as I admire the AI as Normal Technology guys, this article and tweet are, IMO, way way off. To wit, their article accepts subjective probability in principle (their words) but they then build their case on the claim that a credence without a reference class or a model is just “feelings dressed up as numbers.” Those can't both be right.  As I read them, the P(doom) people are working in a tradition, from Ramsey through Jaynes (super important to this group esp Yudkowsky), in which every probability is a degree of belief and a reference class is just one kind of evidence. This to be clear isn’t my take, as I’m more of a Knightian (who a lot of the rationalists disdain, I think) and Elster (who is never cited). But the “Normal Tech” critique has to, well, meet the tradition it's criticizing. I don’t think they do that in this article. Say what you want to about the credence approach, but some of the most important thinkers on statistics built the edifice of it. If you want to say Jaynes, Ramsey, de Finetti, Savage, or Cox et al are wrong, make the case. But it’s not crazy to value them. They are very important thinkers, IMO, and it is not fraudulent to adopt their methods, even if you think it's ultimately wrong. Even on the empirics, giving numbers allows a debate, and as the rats say, you have a number even if you don't offer one (see their criticism of Knight, alas). @random_walker @itaisher

🚢 Decision could come within weeks: Partners in Shell-led LNG Canada could make a final investment decision (FID) as early as October 2026, according to three people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. LNG Canada itself says it hopes to reach an investment decision before year-end.  

📈 Capacity would double: Phase 2 would add another 14 million metric tons per year (mtpa) of LNG export capacity, taking the Kitimat, British Columbia, facility from 14 mtpa to 28 mtpa. 

💰 Massive investment: Canada's Major Projects Office estimates Phase 2 could attract about C$33 billion in private-sector capital. The first phase cost roughly C$40 billion and began shipping LNG in 2025. 

🌏 Asia is a major driver: Reuters reports that LNG buyers, particularly in Asia, are placing greater emphasis on supply security amid Middle East conflict, Red Sea shipping disruptions and uncertainty around the Strait of Hormuz. 🛢️ Pipeline expansion is advancing: Coastal GasLink is simultaneously working on a Phase 2 expansion that would increase pipeline capacity sufficiently to support LNG Canada's additional production. LNG Canada and TC Energy reached commercial agreements earlier this year to advance engineering and execution planning. 

🤝 First Nations participation: Five First Nations have been offered an option to invest up to C$1 billion in a Phase 2 storage tank, giving Indigenous communities a potential equity stake in the expansion. 

🇨🇦 Strategic significance for Canada: The Canadian government says Phase 2 could help Canada become a top-five global LNG exporter and diversify its energy exports beyond the U.S. market. The project is also being advanced as a federal priority through Canada's Major Projects Office.
